docs.text: DiceModders This site is intended for the documentation of DiceKingdoms in order to make modding the game easier. Where to start Playing with mods: Mods Installation . Writing a mod: Project Setup , IL2CPP tips , then the tested Hook recipes . How the game works: start with the Overview and the Turn loop , then one page per phase: Harvest , Disasters , Build phase , Combat , Win conditions . The AI and all numbers in Game data . Islands: Grid , Generation , Save format (island codes). Multiplayer: Networking (what runs on the host, what every player needs) and Lobby, menus and Steam . Interface and visuals: Game UI , Interface behaviour , Rendering , Audio, settings and localization , Developer console . New looks and civilizations: Custom models , Making a civilization , Civilizations in the game code , Civilization models and sprites . Addresses and offsets: Reverse-engineering notes and the Internals reference (game version 1.0.4). Sharing your mod: Publishing a mod .

docs.text: AI AIPlay (a component on the GameState object) runs on the server only . AIPlay.PlayPhase(phaseData, AIState) → AIState ( 0x567640 ) is called once per phase, when the phase ends (at sync) , for every AI island; it dispatches to PlayStart , PlayHarvest , PlayBuild and the combat code. So the AI never acts during a phase, only at its end. Player.AIState (networked): Difficulty , Strategy , TechnologiesToResearch , BuildingToPlace (its plan, kept between phases). Difficulties: PASSIVE 0, PEASANT, BOURGEOIS, GENERAL, KING, SORCERER. The lobby offers Peasant to Sorcerer; Passive is only used by the tutorial . Strategies: MILITARY 0, WONDER 1. WONDER is only allowed when the lobby option Wonder Victory is on. GameState.AddAI adds a bot; matchmaking can fill empty slots with AIs. AIConfiguration A MonoBehaviour asset inside sharedassets1.assets (not a loose file). Changing it needs a plugin (edit the object at runtime). Constant Value Use hammerToKeep 5 shipPerBuilding 2 ships per target building sorcererTowerLimit 2 extra Sorcerer Towers are burnt turnCountLimit 3 early-game rules end after turn 3 topBuildingCountToPlace 6 how far it looks ahead in its build list attackScoreRandomness 200 turnCountBerserk 11 after turn 11 + random(−1..2) it targets Castles Difficulty limitBuildingScore aggressiveness defensiveness maxLavaToClean Passive 0.7 0.9 1 2 Peasant 0.8 1.1 0.8 2 Bourgeois 1.2 1.1 1 2 General 2 1 1.1 2 King 10 1.3 1.2 50 Sorcerer 10 1.2 1.4 50 Each difficulty also has a harvestMultiplier per resource that multiplies the AI's final harvest (for example Peasant: food ×1.5, wood/stone/gold/hammer ×0.9, culture/military ×0.7; Bourgeois: food ×1.5, wood/stone/hammer ×1.1; Sorcerer: food/wood/stone/hammer ×1.7). AI income is not the plain dice result. Scoring weights: soldier 4, archer 8, templar 9, sorcerer 18, requireShip 0.3, guardTower 32, towerUpgrade 72, wall 0.2, inhabitant 0.4, builtResources 2, storedResources 1.2, castle 10. Build orders AIPlay.InitBuildOrders ( 0x564260 ) loads 15 build orders (5 civilizations × culture , wonder , military_macro ) from a text compiled into the game. If the file custom-build-orders.txt exists in the game folder (next to Dice-Kingdoms.exe ), it is read instead (confirmed in game; the log still says "Loaded 15 build orders."). So the AI's build orders can be changed with a text file alone, no plugin needed. Keep the same format: civilization=VIKING weight=2 strategy=MILITARY name=military_macro [ technologies [ UNLOCK_FISHING_SHIP UNLOCK_ARCHERY_RANGE ... ] buildings [ house house church cot cot ... ] ] Building short names: house, cot (Cottage), church, farm, racks (Barracks), dock, land (Land Camp), storage, mill (Windmill), fish (Fishing Ship), guard, cat (Cathedral), university, market, lumber, quarry, archery, wonder, sorcerer. SampleBuildOrder ( 0x568710 ) picks one at random, weighted, among those for the AI's civilization and allowed strategies (an unknown civilization throws). The log line AI <name> has strategy MILITARY and build order military_macro comes from PlayStart . Start phase PlayStart ( 0x567FE0 ) places the start buildings with a spiral from the centre, 4 orientations from a random start, Farms only at Manhattan distance ≥ 15 from the centre , no extra disease risk. Then it picks its strategy and build order. Harvest PlayHarvest ( 0x566620 ), after the AI's dice were rolled, for each re-roll: It predicts the next disaster. If that would be Plague, Disease (after turn 3), Pirates (WONDER AI) or Revolt (MILITARY AI), it re-rolls up to 5 dice without a disaster point, lowest yield first (dice showing a disaster point cannot be re-rolled, for players either). Only before turn 3: food management (re-roll Cottages that gave no food when food is short) and the strategy re-roll (MILITARY: every Barracks die under 3 military; WONDER: none). Its hammer yield is raised so it ends with at least 2 hammers. The yields are multiplied by the difficulty's harvestMultiplier ( HarvestData.SetAIYields ). Passive AI only: military limited to half the highest human's stored military, culture to 1.5 × the highest. Build PlayBuild ( 0x565500 ): Research , if it has an active University: walk its technology list; skip ones not yet learnable; stop at the first learnable one it cannot afford. Clean remains (rebuild-first), burn Sorcerer Towers above the limit (a House is queued for each), build and clean, use the Market, build and clean again. Rubber band: a building score is the cost total of an island's buildings (bulk-placed pieces like Walls do not count). The AI only places a building if own score + building cost ≤ (best human score) × limitBuildingScore . So Peasant and Passive AIs never build more than 80 % / 70 % of the best human's building value; King and Sorcerer are practically unlimited (confirmed in game: a Peasant AI stopped building until the player built more). The score is checked once per round of the build loop, so it can overshoot slightly. Defences: Guard Towers in its list are skipped unless its defence score is below the strongest enemy attack score × defensiveness . Choosing: of the first 6 items in its build list that are unlocked and placeable, the first it can afford and that fits under the rubber band. If it is already winning, it only builds Guard Towers. WONDER AIs reserve a Wonder spot first. Placing ( WhereToPlaceBuilding 0x56AAF0 ): spiral from the centre outwards, all 4 orientations from a random start; Farms only at distance ≥ 15; no extra disease risk up to turn 3. Buildings that profit from neighbours (Land Camp, Cathedral, Windmill, Lumber Camp, Stone Quarry, Fishing Ship) go where they touch the most useful tiles (not placed at all if none); everything else at the first free spot closest to the centre. PlaceBuildingAt clears blocking nature and remains, places the building, and puts a ring of Walls around it: 1 thick around Cathedral, Market, Storage, University and Windmill, 2 around the Wonder. Cleaning: remains of destroyed buildings are cleaned and that building is put at the front of the build list (it rebuilds first). Remains on lava: at most maxLavaToClean per phase. When nothing can be built it cleans one rock (if it has less stone than wood) or tree, not next to its own Quarry / Lumber Camp. Market: MILITARY AIs buy military with all gold above 10, WONDER AIs buy hammers with all gold above 15. Nothing else. Never used by the AI: repairing buildings. Attack At the end of the combat phase (inside PlayPhase ): No attack for a Passive AI, or without soldiers or a free Dock. Ships = min(free Docks, soldiers / ship capacity); targets = max(1, ships / 2). GetWarTarget ( 0x562FA0 ): Stop the winner: if somebody not on its team is about to win, attack their Castle (or Wonder for a wonder win). Otherwise: attack = (0.7 × military + 0.3 × min(military, ship capacity × docks)) × SoldierFactor (SoldierFactor = 18 with Warlocks, 9 with Templars, 8 with archers, else 4). DevelopmentScore = 2 × building cost totals + 1.2 × stored wood, stone, gold, hammers and culture. DefenseScore = military × its SoldierFactor + 32 × Guard Towers + 72 × Guard Towers Up + 0.2 × Walls + 0.4 × active population + 10 × Castles. Candidates: enemies with DefenseScore ≤ attack × aggressiveness and development at least (1 − r²) × the best (r random). One is picked at random, weighted exp((development − defense) / 200). Target buildings: after the berserk turn its Castle(s); before, the richest-loot buildings (not Farm, Wall, Castle, towers, Wonder, Sorcerer Tower). It sends ranged units if unlocked (melee Templars if it has Templars but not Warlocks), full ships, spread over the targets; the drop point is the target building.

docs.text: Audio, settings, localization and tutorial Audio Piece What it is Sound (ScriptableObject, 48 assets) clips[] , mixerGroup , minVolume / maxVolume , minPitch / maxPitch , loop AudioSources (static instance ) a pool of 2048 AudioSources AudioSources.AllocatedSource the handle Play returns: source + ticket ; an old handle can never stop a sound that reused the source Main mixer Master › Main › Effects, Music, Ambient, Interface; exposed Main_Volume , Effects_Volume , Music_Volume , Ambient_Volume , Interface_Volume AudioSources.Play(sound, position?) ( 0x580C20 ) takes the first free source (none free → error, no sound), 3D at the position or 2D without one, random pitch and volume in the sound's ranges, a random clip , and plays it. Music Music (match scene): calm track per civilization (Europe 6 clips, Middle East 3, Viking 9, Ancient 9, Maya 6), combat, decisive combat, winning and losing tracks. Music.get_Track ( 0x590F70 ), every frame: Win phase with a result → winning if the winner is on your team, else losing. Combat phase, 5 s into the fight → decisive if somebody could win this turn ( WinPhase.CheckWin() at phase start), else combat. Otherwise the calm track of your civilization. When a song ends, a new random clip of the same track starts (a shuffled playlist). Changes crossfade over 2 s . The main menu has its own menuMusic . Volume Five sliders (0–100) in the settings. Each writes its mixer parameter as dB = clamp(20 × log10(value / 100) + offset, −80, 0) : Slider Offset Default Main 0 70 Effects +6 100 Music −8 50 Ambient 0 100 Interface +5 100 Ambience: the sea, and a night-nature loop that only plays at night (see Rendering ). For mods: AudioSources.instance.Play(sound, null) plays any Sound ; keep the handle to stop it. Music can be replaced by changing the clips of the Music-* assets or by a postfix on Music.get_Track . Settings and saved data The game saves only four settings files ( video , audio , input , game , JSON) and the flag file GameSettings/.did-tutorial . There are no save games, no PlayerPrefs and no Steam stats, achievements or leaderboards. SettingSets ( localFolder = "GameSettings" , path relative to the game folder): Set Stored video always the local file GameSettings/video.json audio, input, game Steam Cloud when Steam runs, otherwise the local file Save when the settings window closes ( SettingSetsInterface.OnDisable ): each set is exported and stored. Load at start: a cloud set with Steam running is read from Steam Cloud only (missing → defaults, no fallback to the local copy); otherwise the local file or defaults. Defaults: video quality Normal, full screen mode 2, 1920×1080, frame limit 144, VSync on; audio as above; input bindings (rotate /Keyboard/r , mirror /Keyboard/t , keep placing /Keyboard/shift , scoreboard /Keyboard/tab , …); game language 0. For a mod's own settings a BepInEx config file is easiest. To use Steam Cloud like the game: SettingSets.Store(true, "GameSettings/mymod.json", bytes) / SettingSets.Get(true, ...) . How the settings window is built: Interface behaviour . Tutorial ("Training") Main menu → Training → MainMenu.LoadTraining : writes .did-tutorial to Steam Cloud as soon as it starts (the "recommend tutorial" hint is hidden from then on), adds two Passive AIs (the only use of that difficulty) and marks the match as training. Training (in the match scene) has TrainingStep children with TrainingObjective s; all the data is in the scene: # Step Objectives 1 Initial buildings Castle, 3 Cottages, Farm, Dock 2 Get more dice 2 Cottages, 2 Houses 3 Stable food supply 2 Farms 4 Culture a Church; 12 culture 5 See opponents' progress open the scoreboard 6 Military Barracks; 8 military 7 Attack a Dock; press Ready in combat; pillage once 8 Research University; research Storage; build a Storage 9 Win military win At the start every building button and Ready are hidden and combat phases are skipped ; each step shows the buttons it needs, and the Pillage step turns combat on. One-time hints ( ConfirmModal.OpenInformation ) explain the harvest, disasters, attack, pillage, starvation and the University. Localization Unity Localization with SmartFormat, string tables in Addressables bundles, 421 keys × 6 languages. Game code goes through StructuredTextStaticReferences.instance ( LocalizeString(key) ). Language at start ( Localization.asset startup selectors): SteamLocaleSelector.GetStartupLocale ( 0x550170 ), only with Steam: english → en; schinese, tchinese → zh; french → fr; russian → ru; ukrainian → ru ; anything else, German included → en . Fallback en . So a German Steam client starts in English, and a Ukrainian one in Russian although a Ukrainian table exists. Language setting ( GameSettings.language , Steam Cloud): 0 Steam default (selectors run again), 1 English, 2 French, 3 Chinese (simplified), 4 Russian, 5 German. There is no Ukrainian entry; only a mod can select it ( LocalizationSettings.SelectedLocale ). Texts are StructuredText with ITextElement.Localized(key, args) : the translation can contain the same icon tokens and {a.N} argument slots (see Interface behaviour ). Rendered text is cached per locale and labels redraw when the language changes. For mods: add entries to the string table at runtime ( LocalizationSettings.StringDatabase.GetTable(...) → AddEntry ) for the language in use (and again when it changes), or write your own StructuredText ; icon tokens work without localization. The startup quirks can be fixed with a postfix on SteamLocaleSelector.GetStartupLocale .

docs.text: Build phase During the build phase the client plans actions. Each one goes to the server ( [ServerRPC] PlanActionRPC(BuildData.Action) ), the server stores it and echoes it to the other clients ( PlanActionClientRPC ). The checks and resource changes happen in BuildData.DoAction , either right away (on a Preview island) or at sync in BuildPhase.ApplyChanges . Action types BuildData.Action.Type : # Type Public method Notes 0 REPAIR_BUILDING RepairBuilding(id) 0x62B1E0 costs toolCost (1 hammer), restores repairToolAmount (60) HP, up to the type's maximum 1 BURN_BUILDING BurnBuilding(id) 0x6282C0 costs toolCost 2 CLEAN_TILE CleanTile(pos) 0x628AB0 costs toolCost ; gives resources back (below) 3 PLACE_BUILDING PlaceBuilding(b) 0x62A920 4 PLACE_BUILDING_BULK PlaceBuildingBulk(b[]) 0x62A860 walls (bulk size 10) 5 BUY_RESOURCE BuyResource(marketId, res) 0x628340 needs a Market 6 LEARN_TECHNOLOGY LearnTechnology(universityId, tech) 0x62A1A0 needs a University 7 SEND_RESOURCES SendResources(target, amount) 0x62B300 to another player; arrives 1:1 8 RECEIVE_RESOURCES ReceiveResources(src, amount) server side of 7 Action struct: type 0x0 , position (int2) 0x4 , buildingId 0xC , building 0x10 , buildings[] 0x38 , resource 0x40 , technology 0x48 , resourceAmount 0x50 , player 0x70 . Planning The public methods only fill an Action and call PlanAction ( 0x62AB20 ): Return false if the build phase is not ACTIVE : no actions are accepted after the timer ends. If this island's BuildData.Preview is true, run DoAction now; if it fails, the action is dropped. The owner sends PlanActionRPC to the server; the server sends PlanActionClientRPC to everybody except the owner. Each side calls PlanAction again. Append the action to the island's action list ( BuildIslandState.Actions ). On the server, SEND_RESOURCES also calls ReceiveResources on the target's BuildData right away. Committing BuildPhase.ApplyChanges ( 0x62C6C0 ), at sync: for every island, every stored action whose island is not Preview goes through DoAction ; failed actions are skipped silently . Successful placements and technologies are counted for the game log (hammer icon followed by NxBuilding , culture icon followed by the technologies). So the server checks every action, but for islands it does not preview it checks them only at sync. Preview: instant or at sync PhaseData.Preview decides whether this machine applies an island's actions the moment they arrive (true) or only at the end of the phase (false). It has nothing to do with the camera. PhaseData.Enter ( 0xE60440 ) sets it for every island, on every machine, at the start of every phase (and on rejoin): The local machine controls the island's owner ( Player.IsInitialOwner ) → true (your own island). Else, on the server, if the owner is an AI → true (the host runs the AIs). Else, in team mode : true for teammates ( Team.Same(owner, Player.Local) ), false for enemies. Else (free-for-all): Player.Local.IsDefeated : false while you are alive, true for every island once you are defeated (spectator). Island Its changes appear on your screen Your own instantly AI islands, when you host instantly Teammates' (team mode) instantly Other human players' when the build phase ends Every island, after you are defeated instantly In a free-for-all with other humans you do not see what they build until the phase ends, and they see your buildings the same way. On the host, a remote human's island is not previewed either; the host checks and applies it at sync like everybody else. (Confirmed in game for the host with AI islands: all previewed.) Checks and effects FixAction (inlined at the start of DoAction 0x628BA0 ): a single placed building's type goes through UpgradedBuildingType (Guard Tower → Guard Tower Up once the upgrade is learnt), and every placed building gets SetNewlyBuilt(turnCounter) . # Checks (in order) Effect 0 Repair can pay toolCost ; building exists; health < type.health pay; IslandGrid.RepairBuilding(id, repairToolAmount) = min(health + 60, max) 1 Burn can pay toolCost ; building exists pay; IslandGrid.RemoveBuilding(id) 2 Clean can pay toolCost ; CanRemoveNature(pos) or CanRemoveRemains(pos) pay; clean (below) 3 Place CanBuildType(type) ; IslandGrid.CanPlaceBuilding add the building; pay type.cost 4 Bulk all the same type; CanBuildType ; can pay cost × n ; every building passes CanPlaceBuilding add all; pay cost × n , n = ceil(count / bulkSize) 5 Buy an offer for the resource exists; can pay its cost; storage of that resource not full ; the Market was not placed this turn ; building active and a Market pay offer.cost ; add offer.amount × TradeFactor (capped by storage) 6 Learn Statistics.IsTechnologyLearnable ; can pay; the University was not placed this turn; building active and a University pay tech.cost ; Statistics.LearnTechnology 7 Send can pay amount remove amount 8 Receive – add amount A Market or University placed this turn cannot be used until the next build phase ( JustPlacedBuilding : a single PLACE_BUILDING with that id in this turn's list). Market: TradeFactor (Trade Efficiency) multiplies the amount received , not the price, and applies in the same phase it is learnt. Offers: 1 gold → 2 food, 1 wood, 1 stone, 1 military or 1 hammer; ×2 with Trade Efficiency (confirmed in game). The trade happens inside DoAction ; BuildData.BuyResource is not on this path, so a hook there does not see trades. Bulk: the buildings inside one bulk action are not checked against each other. The normal client never sends overlapping ones ( BuildingBulkPlacer skips taken positions). IslandGrid.AddBuilding re-checks only inside Assert.IsTrue , and Unity's Assert only logs by default. A building's id is its anchor position: Building.id = (y << 16) | x . Check functions Function Rule BuildingType.IsBuildable 0x5F0F10 cost != ZERO . The Castle has no cost, so it can only be placed in the start phase. BuildData.CanBuildType 0x628760 IsBuildable and Unlocked(type) and the demo rule (Steam demo: only tier 1 or Storage) and can pay type.cost . BuildData.Unlocked 0x62BAA0 Locked if an UnlockBuildingTechnology for this type exists and is not learnt. An upgraded type (Guard Tower Up) only through its upgrade technology. The Wonder is locked when the lobby option Wonder Victory is off. BuildData.UpgradedBuildingType 0x62BE70 Guard Tower → Guard Tower Up once upgradeGuardTower is learnt. CanAffordBulk / BulkCount BulkCount(type, n) = n < 1 ? 0 : (n − 1) / bulkSize + 1 . CanRepair 0x6289E0 building exists and health < type.health . CanBurn 0x628830 building exists, nothing else. CanRemoveNature 0x6288B0 nature is TREE, ROCK, SCORCHED_EARTH or LAVA (its own check; NatureTile.Cleanable is not called). CanRemoveRemains 0x628960 there are remains on the tile. IslandGrid.CanPlaceBuilding 0x6143A0 For every tile: inside the grid; no building; ground WATER for the type's water tiles, otherwise GRASS or PIER ; no nature except FLOWER (removed when placed); no remains. Sand, cliffs and meteorite ground are never buildable. Water tiles ( localPositionsInWater ): Dock 11 of 12 tiles (the pier), Fishing Ship both tiles, Lighthouse all 4 tiles (2×2 on water). Fish block placement : fish is a nature tile, so a Dock, Fishing Ship or Lighthouse cannot cover it. Scorched earth and lava block building until cleaned. Cleaning a tile DoCleanTile : Remains on the tile: reward = the remains' remainsReward ; the remains are removed. Nature ( NatureYields 0x62A270 ), ×2 with Double Clean Tile : Nature Yield Tree 1 wood Rock 1 stone Scorched earth 1 disaster point Lava 1 random: wood, stone or disaster point, fixed per tile (hash of the position, seed y*128 + x + 62 ) Flowers and fish are never cleaned. IslandGrid.RemoveNature also turns meteorite ground back into grass , so one clean makes a lava tile buildable again. 3. The reward is added (capped by storage) and onCleanTile(position, nature, amount) fires. Technologies Classes: UnlockBuildingTechnology , AddRollTechnology (+1 re-roll), DoubleCleanTileTechnology , ReplaceBuildings (Guard Tower upgrade), ReplaceSoldiers (Templars replace Soldiers, Warlocks replace Archers), RitualsTechnology , ShipCapacityTechnology ( Statistics.ShipCapacity ), TradeEfficiencyTechnology ( Statistics.TradeFactor ). Costs: Game data ; trees: Civilizations in the game code . Guard Tower upgrade: ReplaceBuildings.OnLearn ( 0x621650 ) replaces every Guard Tower on the island with a Guard Tower Up at the same place, keeping its health number (a damaged tower is not healed). New Guard Towers are placed as the upgraded type from then on. Burning the Castle Nothing stops it: CanBurn only checks that the building exists and is not even called by the UI; the burn button ( BuildInterface ) and the building selector have no type filter. So a player can burn their own Castle in the build phase for 1 hammer. What happens then: Win conditions .

docs.text: During the build phase the client plans actions. Each one goes to the server ( [ServerRPC] PlanActionRPC(BuildData.Action) ), the server stores it and echoes it to the other clients ( PlanActionClientRPC ). The checks and resource changes happen in BuildData.DoAction , either right away (on a Preview island) or at sync in BuildPhase.ApplyChanges .

docs.text: The public methods only fill an Action and call PlanAction ( 0x62AB20 ): Return false if the build phase is not ACTIVE : no actions are accepted after the timer ends. If this island's BuildData.Preview is true, run DoAction now; if it fails, the action is dropped. The owner sends PlanActionRPC to the server; the server sends PlanActionClientRPC to everybody except the owner. Each side calls PlanAction again. Append the action to the island's action list ( BuildIslandState.Actions ). On the server, SEND_RESOURCES also calls ReceiveResources on the target's BuildData right away.

docs.text: Buildings BuildingType Each building kind is a BuildingType object held in a BuildingTypes collection (referenced by RulesBuilding ). The index in BuildingTypes.Types is the id used in save files and island codes . namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingType { public BuildingTypeName name ; public int2 [] localPositions ; public int2 [] localPositionsInWater ; public HeightOverride [] heightOverrides ; public BuildingVisual visualPrefab ; public ResourceAmount storageCapacity ; public ResourceAmount cost ; public int tier ; public int bulkSize ; public int health ; public bool fortification ; public bool garrison ; public ResourceAmount pillageReward ; public ResourceAmount remainsReward ; public Opt < Tower > tower ; public bool hasEffectDescription ; public string DisplayName { get ; } public bool IsBuildable { get ; } public bool HasEffectDescription { get ; } public bool IsWaterPosition ( int2 localPosition ); public float? GetHeightOverride ( int2 localPosition ); public override string ToString (); public virtual bool Equals ( BuildingType other ); } Fields. name - the type identifier from the BuildingTypeName enum. localPositions - the tiles the building occupies, in building-local coordinates. localPositionsInWater - footprint variant for water. heightOverrides - per-tile visual height overrides. visualPrefab - the visual prefab. storageCapacity - storage capacity granted by the building. cost - building cost. tier - technology tier (1–3). bulkSize - bulk placement size. health - maximum health. fortification / garrison - "fortification" and "garrison" flags. pillageReward / remainsReward - rewards for pillaging and for being reduced to remains. tower - optional tower data. hasEffectDescription - whether an effect description is shown. Properties. DisplayName returns the localized name. IsBuildable determines whether the type appears in the build menu. HasEffectDescription wraps the field. Methods. IsWaterPosition checks whether a local offset is a water tile for this type. GetHeightOverride returns the height override for a specific tile. Offsets are build specific Offsets and RVAs on this page come from one game build (see Internals Reference ). Field names are stable; numbers may move after a game update. Field Type Offset Notes id int 0x10 The type id (equals the index in BuildingTypes.Types ) localPositions int2[] 0x18 Footprint, in building-local coordinates localPositionsInWater int2[] 0x20 Footprint variant used in water cost block struct 0x58 - 0x74 resource cost tier int 0x78 1-3, see the table below health int 0x80 Maximum health Class hierarchy Not every building type is a plain BuildingType . The game uses a small hierarchy of subclasses to attach specialized behaviour: BuildingType (base) BuildingTypeHousing - housing (rolls a die for yield) BuildingTypeCastle - castle Cottage, Church, House, Barracks, Sorcerer Tower BuildingTypeProducer (abstract) BuildingTypeProducerFixed - Farm BuildingTypeProducerNature - Lumber Camp, Stone Quarry, Fishing Ship BuildingTypeProducerAmplifier - Cathedral, Windmill, Market BuildingTypeDock - Dock BuildingTypeHospital - Hospital BuildingTypeSoldierFamily - Archery Range BuildingTypeTech - University BuildingTypeWonder - Wonder BuildingTypeApplyModifierInRange - Lighthouse BuildingTypeLandExtension - Land Camp (implements IBuildingTypeUpdateOnHarvest ) Plain BuildingType : Wall, Guard Tower, Guard Tower Up, Storage Specialized types BuildingTypeHousing Residential buildings that produce a unit and yield resources via a die roll. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeHousing : BuildingType { public ResourceAmount [] possibleYields ; public Color diceColor ; public Unit . Type unitType ; public Dice dicePrefab ; } Fields. possibleYields - possible die outcomes. diceColor - die color. unitType - the unit type produced. dicePrefab - die prefab. BuildingTypeCastle Castle. Extends BuildingTypeHousing without adding any fields of its own. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeCastle : BuildingTypeHousing { } BuildingTypeProducer Abstract base class for all resource producers. Defines a single abstract method. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game; [Serializable] public abstract class BuildingTypeProducer : BuildingType { public abstract ResourceAmount Yield ( Island island , Building building ); } Methods. Yield returns the amount of resources produced for a specific building on a specific island. Each subclass implements it differently. BuildingTypeProducerFixed A producer with a fixed yield - for example, a farm. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeProducerFixed : BuildingTypeProducer { public ResourceAmount yield ; public override ResourceAmount Yield ( Island island , Building building ); } Fields. yield - always the same amount of resources, regardless of surroundings. Yield simply returns yield . BuildingTypeProducerNature A producer whose yield depends on nearby nature tiles - lumber camp, stone quarry, fishing ship. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeProducerNature : BuildingTypeProducer { public Resource yieldResource ; public NatureTile natureTile ; public int tilesNeeded ; public Resource YieldResource { get ; } public NatureTile NatureTile { get ; } public int TilesNeeded { get ; } public int NatureNeighborsCount ( Island island , Building building ); public override ResourceAmount Yield ( Island island , Building building ); public float AverageYield ( Island island , Building [] buildings ); } Fields. yieldResource - which resource is produced. natureTile - which nature tile is counted. tilesNeeded - how many such tiles are needed for full output. Methods. NatureNeighborsCount counts the nature tiles of the required type around the building. Yield multiplies that count by the base rate. AverageYield computes the average yield across an array of buildings - used in UI and for previews. BuildingTypeProducerAmplifier Amplifier - boosts the production of another building type. For example, windmill, market, cathedral. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeProducerAmplifier : BuildingTypeProducer { public BuildingTypes buildingTypes ; public Resource yieldResource ; public BuildingTypeName amplifiedBuildingTypeName ; public int amplifyFactor ; public int amplifyFactorProximityBonus ; public Resource YieldResource { get ; } public int AmplifyFactor { get ; } public int ProximityBonus { get ; } public BuildingType AmplifiedBuildingType { get ; } public int AmplifiedCount ( Island island ); public int AmplifiedProximityCount ( Island island , Building building ); public float AverageAmplifiedProximityCount ( Island island , Building [] buildings ); public override ResourceAmount Yield ( Island island , Building building ); public float AverageFactor ( Island island , Building [] buildings ); } Fields. buildingTypes - the type registry. yieldResource - the resource produced. amplifiedBuildingTypeName - which building type is amplified. amplifyFactor - the base amplification factor. amplifyFactorProximityBonus - bonus for being near the amplified building. Methods. AmplifiedCount counts all amplified buildings on the island. AmplifiedProximityCount - those within range. Yield combines the base factor and the proximity bonus. AverageFactor returns the average multiplier across an array of buildings. BuildingTypeSoldierFamily Archery range - binds the building to a unit family. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeSoldierFamily : BuildingType { public Unit . Family soldierFamily ; public Unit . Family SoldierFamily { get ; } } Fields. soldierFamily - the unit family produced by the building. BuildingTypeTech namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeTech : BuildingType { public int unlocksTier ; } BuildingTypeApplyModifierInRange Lighthouse - applies a modifier to buildings of a specific type within range. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeApplyModifierInRange : BuildingType { public BuildingTypes buildingTypes ; public int range ; public BuildingModifier modifier ; public BuildingTypeName affectedBuildingType ; public int Range { get ; } public BuildingModifier Modifier { get ; } public BuildingType AffectedBuildingType { get ; } public bool Affects ( Building source , Building target ); public static bool HasModifier ( Island island , BuildingModifier modifier , Building building ); } Fields. buildingTypes - the type registry. range - the range of effect. modifier - the modifier applied (see BuildingModifier ). affectedBuildingType - the building type the modifier acts on. Methods. Affects checks whether a specific target is affected by the source. HasModifier - a static helper: whether a building on the island has the given modifier. BuildingTypeLandExtension Land camp - extends land on each harvest. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeLandExtension : BuildingType , IBuildingTypeUpdateOnHarvest { public int range ; public int tilesPerTurn ; public void ApplyHarvest ( Island island , Building building ); public int2 [] AffectedPositions ( Island island , Building building ); } Fields. range - the extension radius. tilesPerTurn - how many tiles are added per harvest. Methods. ApplyHarvest is called by the engine after the harvest phase. AffectedPositions returns the list of tiles that will be affected. IBuildingTypeUpdateOnHarvest Interface for types that react to harvest. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; public interface IBuildingTypeUpdateOnHarvest { void ApplyHarvest ( Island island , Building building ); } Methods. ApplyHarvest is called for every building of that type after the harvest phase completes. HeightOverride Per-tile visual height override. public struct HeightOverride { public int2 position ; public float height ; } Fields. position - the tile's local coordinate. height - the visual height at that tile. BuildingModifier Modifier applied by effect buildings. Currently only one exists. public enum BuildingModifier { DOUBLE_FISH } Values. DOUBLE_FISH - doubles fish production for buildings within range. Type ids Ids 0-20 are alphabetical by display name; 21-23 were added later and sit at the end. There is no in-game build menu - buildings are panels at the bottom of the screen; picking one makes it follow the cursor until you left-click. Id Name Tiles Tier Max HP 0 Archery Range 5 2 60 1 Barracks 6 1 60 2 Castle 16 1 200 3 Cathedral 6 2 40 4 Church 3 1 15 5 Cottage 2 1 10 6 Dock 12 1 50 7 Farm 8 1 15 8 Guard Tower 4 2 40 9 Guard Tower Up 4 2 40 10 Hospital 5 2 40 11 House 3 1 15 12 Lumber Camp 4 3 20 13 Market 4 3 10 14 Sorcerer Tower 3 2 20 15 Stone Quarry 3 3 20 16 Storage 6 2 20 17 University 7 1 50 18 Wall 1 1 50 19 Windmill 4 2 20 20 Wonder 15 3 150 21 Fishing Ship 2 2 30 22 Lighthouse 4 3 50 23 Land Camp 4 3 20 BuildingTypeName enum The BuildingTypeName enum lists all types in the same order as the ids. public enum BuildingTypeName { ARCHERY_RANGE , BARRACKS , CASTLE , CATHEDRAL , CHURCH , COTTAGE , DOCK , FARM , GUARD_TOWER , GUARD_TOWER_UP , HOSPITAL , HOUSE , LUMBER_CAMP , MARKET , SORCERER_TOWER , STONE_QUARRY , STORAGE , UNIVERSITY , WALL , WINDMILL , WONDER , FISHING_SHIP , LIGHTHOUSE , LAND_CAMP } Footprint and rotation GridTransform.TransformVector rotates by orient (0-3) in 90 degree steps, then mirror flips X: orient (cos, sin) 0 (1, 0) 1 (0, 1) 2 (-1, 0) 3 (0, -1) static ( int x , int y ) Transform ( int dx , int dy , int orient , bool mirror ) { int [] cos = { 1 , 0 , - 1 , 0 }; int [] sin = { 0 , 1 , 0 , - 1 }; int c = cos [(( orient % 4 ) + 4 ) % 4 ], s = sin [(( orient % 4 ) + 4 ) % 4 ]; int nx = dx * c - dy * s ; int ny = dx * s + dy * c ; if ( mirror ) nx = - nx ; return ( nx , ny ); } IEnumerable < ( int x , int y ) > Footprint ( BuildingType t , int bx , int by , int orient , bool mirror ) => t . localPositions . Select ( o => { var ( x , y ) = Transform ( o . x , o . y , orient , mirror ); return ( bx + x , by + y ); }); Logic. The Transform function rotates the local offset by orient * 90° counter-clockwise, then, if mirror = true , reflects the result across X. Footprint applies this transformation to all localPositions and adds the world position of the building. A wrapper over an int that identifies a specific building. OfPosition creates an id from a grid position - useful when you need to find a building by coordinate without scanning the island's full building list. Equals , GetHashCode , the == / != operators and CompareTo make Id a full-fledged key for dictionaries and sorting. BuildingTypes (registry) A ScriptableObject-like registry holding every BuildingType . namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; public class BuildingTypes { public BuildingType castle ; public BuildingType wall ; public BuildingType farm ; public BuildingType cottage ; public BuildingType house ; public BuildingType church ; public BuildingType barracks ; public BuildingType guardTower ; public BuildingType guardTowerUp ; public BuildingType storage ; public BuildingType lumberCamp ; public BuildingType stoneQuarry ; public BuildingType windmill ; public BuildingType market ; public BuildingType cathedral ; public BuildingType archeryRange ; public BuildingType dock ; public BuildingType hospital ; public BuildingType sorcererTower ; public BuildingType university ; public BuildingType wonder ; public BuildingType fishingShip ; public BuildingType lighthouse ; public BuildingType landCamp ; public BuildingType [] Types { get { } } public Dictionary < string , BuildingType > typesByName { get { } } public BuildingType Get ( BuildingTypeName name ) { } public void Init () { } public void OnEnable () { } } Fields. docs.text: Each building kind is a BuildingType object held in a BuildingTypes collection (referenced by RulesBuilding ). The index in BuildingTypes.Types is the id used in save files and island codes . namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingType { public BuildingTypeName name ; public int2 [] localPositions ; public int2 [] localPositionsInWater ; public HeightOverride [] heightOverrides ; public BuildingVisual visualPrefab ; public ResourceAmount storageCapacity ; public ResourceAmount cost ; public int tier ; public int bulkSize ; public int health ; public bool fortification ; public bool garrison ; public ResourceAmount pillageReward ; public ResourceAmount remainsReward ; public Opt < Tower > tower ; public bool hasEffectDescription ; public string DisplayName { get ; } public bool IsBuildable { get ; } public bool HasEffectDescription { get ; } public bool IsWaterPosition ( int2 localPosition ); public float? GetHeightOverride ( int2 localPosition ); public override string ToString (); public virtual bool Equals ( BuildingType other ); } Fields. name - the type identifier from the BuildingTypeName enum. localPositions - the tiles the building occupies, in building-local coordinates. localPositionsInWater - footprint variant for water. heightOverrides - per-tile visual height overrides. visualPrefab - the visual prefab. storageCapacity - storage capacity granted by the building. cost - building cost. tier - technology tier (1–3). bulkSize - bulk placement size. health - maximum health. fortification / garrison - "fortification" and "garrison" flags. pillageReward / remainsReward - rewards for pillaging and for being reduced to remains. tower - optional tower data. hasEffectDescription - whether an effect description is shown. Properties. DisplayName returns the localized name. IsBuildable determines whether the type appears in the build menu. HasEffectDescription wraps the field. Methods. IsWaterPosition checks whether a local offset is a water tile for this type. GetHeightOverride returns the height override for a specific tile. Offsets are build specific Offsets and RVAs on this page come from one game build (see Internals Reference ). Field names are stable; numbers may move after a game update. docs.text: Not every building type is a plain BuildingType . docs.text: A producer whose yield depends on nearby nature tiles - lumber camp, stone quarry, fishing ship. namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] public class BuildingTypeProducerNature : BuildingTypeProducer { public Resource yieldResource ; public NatureTile natureTile ; public int tilesNeeded ; public Resource YieldResource { get ; } public NatureTile NatureTile { get ; } public int TilesNeeded { get ; } public int NatureNeighborsCount ( Island island , Building building ); public override ResourceAmount Yield ( Island island , Building building ); public float AverageYield ( Island island , Building [] buildings ); } Fields. yieldResource - which resource is produced. natureTile - which nature tile is counted. tilesNeeded - how many such tiles are needed for full output. Methods. NatureNeighborsCount counts the nature tiles of the required type around the building. Yield multiplies that count by the base rate. docs.text: GridTransform.TransformVector rotates by orient (0-3) in 90 degree steps, then mirror flips X: orient (cos, sin) 0 (1, 0) 1 (0, 1) 2 (-1, 0) 3 (0, -1) static ( int x , int y ) Transform ( int dx , int dy , int orient , bool mirror ) { int [] cos = { 1 , 0 , - 1 , 0 }; int [] sin = { 0 , 1 , 0 , - 1 }; int c = cos [(( orient % 4 ) + 4 ) % 4 ], s = sin [(( orient % 4 ) + 4 ) % 4 ]; int nx = dx * c - dy * s ; int ny = dx * s + dy * c ; if ( mirror ) nx = - nx ; return ( nx , ny ); } IEnumerable < ( int x , int y ) > Footprint ( BuildingType t , int bx , int by , int orient , bool mirror ) => t . localPositions . Select ( o => { var ( x , y ) = Transform ( o . x , o . y , orient , mirror ); return ( bx + x , by + y ); }); Logic. The Transform function rotates the local offset by orient * 90° counter-clockwise, then, if mirror = true , reflects the result across X. Footprint applies this transformation to all localPositions and adds the world position of the building. Local offsets (dx, dy) per type, exactly as read from localPositions : Archery Range [[0,0],[-1,0],[0,-1],[-1,-1],[-1,-2]] Barracks [[-1,1],[0,1],[0,0],[0,-1],[1,0],[1,-1]] Castle [[-1,-1],[-1,0],[-1,1],[-1,2],[0,-1],[0,0],[0,1],[0,2],[1,-1],[1,0],[1,1],[1,2],[2,-1],[2,0],[2,1],[2,2]] Cathedral [[1,0],[0,0],[-1,0],[-2,0],[0,1],[0,-1]] Church [[0,0],[-1,0],[-2,0]] Cottage [[0,0],[0,1]] Dock [[0,0],[1,0],[2,0],[2,1],[3,0],[3,1],[4,-1],[4,0],[4,1],[5,-1],[5,0],[5,1]] Farm [[0,1],[0,0],[0,-1],[0,-2],[1,1],[1,0],[1,-1],[1,-2]] Guard Tower [[0,0],[-1,0],[0,-1],[-1,-1]] Guard Tower Up [[0,0],[-1,0],[0,-1],[-1,-1]] Hospital [[0,0],[-1,0],[1,0],[0,-1],[0,1]] House [[0,0],[-1,0],[0,-1]] Lumber Camp [[0,0],[-1,0],[-1,1],[-2,1]] Market [[0,0],[1,0],[1,1],[0,1]] Sorcerer Tower [[0,0],[1,0],[0,1]] Stone Quarry [[0,0],[0,1],[1,0]] Storage [[0,0],[1,0],[0,-1],[1,-1],[0,1],[1,1]] University [[0,1],[0,0],[0,-1],[1,1],[1,-1],[2,1],[2,-1]] Wall [[0,0]] Windmill [[0,0],[-1,0],[-1,1],[0,1]] Wonder [[3,-1],[3,0],[3,1],[2,-1],[2,0],[2,1],[1,-1],[1,0],[1,1],[0,-1],[0,0],[0,1],[-1,-1],[-1,0],[-1,1]] Fishing Ship [[0,0],[0,1]] Lighthouse [[0,0],[-1,0],[0,-1],[-1,-1]] Land Camp [[0,0],[1,1],[0,1],[-1,1]]

docs.text: Civilization assets: models and sprites What a civilization looks like is a set of prefabs (3D models) and sprites (icons). The names below were listed from the game's loaded assets ( Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll , game version 1.0.4), so they are the real names. How the game picks them is in Civilizations in the game code ; how a mod supplies its own is in Making a civilization . Models (prefabs) Every model name is <thing> <civilization> , with the civilization written Europe , Middle East , Viking , Ancient or Maya . A mod civilization replaces any of them with its own prefab; whatever it leaves out keeps the European one. Buildings ( BuildingVisual ) One prefab per building type and civilization, 24 types x 5 civilizations. The European one is the default ( BuildingType.visualPrefab ): Archery Range , Barracks , Castle , Cathedral , Church , Cottage , Dock , Farm , Fishing Ship , Guard Tower , Guard Tower Up , Hospital , House , Land Camp , Lighthouse , Lumber Camp , Market , Sorcerer Tower , Stone Quarry , Storage , University , Wall , Windmill , Wonder . Example: Castle Maya , Guard Tower Up Viking . The building type enum ( BuildingTypeName ) has the same 24 names in upper case with underscores, in this order: ARCHERY_RANGE , BARRACKS , CASTLE , CATHEDRAL , CHURCH , COTTAGE , DOCK , FARM , GUARD_TOWER , GUARD_TOWER_UP , HOSPITAL , HOUSE , LUMBER_CAMP , MARKET , SORCERER_TOWER , STONE_QUARRY , STORAGE , UNIVERSITY , WALL , WINDMILL , WONDER , FISHING_SHIP , LIGHTHOUSE , LAND_CAMP . A few buildings have several scene instances named Cottage Maya (1) , House Ancient (2) and so on. Those are variants placed in the scene, not separate prefabs. Units ( UnitVisual ) Ten unit types, each in every civilization: Archer , Bourgeois , General , King , Peasant , Priest , Soldier , Sorcerer , Templar , Warlock (example: Soldier Europe ). The skin registry also holds Inhabitant King <civ> and Inhabitant Sorcerer <civ> models. Ship ( ShipVisual ) Ship Europe , Ship Middle East , Ship Viking , Ship Ancient , Ship Maya . Nature ( NatureVisualHub ) Per biome ( Plains , Desert , Snow , Mediterranean , Jungle ): Tree <biome> , Rock <biome> , Flower <biome> . Beyond those: Fish Plains , Lava and Scorched Earth (these have no biome of their own). Rock Mediterranean was not found in memory. Inner cliffs ( InnerCliffVisualHub ) Five shapes per biome: Inner Cliff Main 3x3 , Inner Cliff Main 2x2 , Inner Cliff Extension 2x2 , Inner Cliff Extension 1x2 , Inner Cliff Extension 1x1 , followed by the biome ( Plains , Desert , Snow , Jungle ). No Mediterranean cliff hubs were found: the Mediterranean biome seems to reuse another biome's. Skin variants ( SkinVariant ) Every prefab above that the skin registry swaps carries a SkinVariant component with the biome, civilization and variant name it stands for. That component and the registry's entries are what SkinRegistry.GetSkinVariant reads. A mod does not need to touch either: ModCivilization.Skins swaps the result of the lookup. Sprites The game has about 1,900 sprites. Most are icons that exist once per player colour. Player colours Twelve colours, used as the last word of an icon name: blue , brown , carribean (sic), cyan , green , grey , ivory , orange , pink , purple , red , yellow . Building icons building-icon-<building>-<civilization>-<colour> , with the words of the name joined by - , for example building-icon-archery-range-ancient-blue . BuildingVisual.Icon(PlayerColor) returns the sprite at the colour index, so a building visual needs 12 sprites in colour order . The dump lists 120 building/civilization pairs, each with a -red sprite; only some pairs (walls and guard towers in every civilization, and most Viking and Ancient buildings) also have the other eleven colours as separate sprites, so check the dump for the pair you copy. The icons are packed in one atlas per civilization ( Buildings Europe Atlas , ... Middle East ... , ... Viking ... , ... Maya ... , ... Ancient ... ), 256x256 each. Unit icons unit-icon-<unit>-<civilization>-<colour> , for example unit-icon-archer-ancient-blue , 256x256, one atlas per civilization ( Units <civ> Atlas ). About 325 distinct unit sprites; every unit has a -red one and many have the other colours too. UnitVisual.Icon(PlayerColor) works the same way as for buildings. Everything else Group Names Resources food , wood , stone , gold , hammer , culture , military , research , population , trade-efficiency Disasters plague , drought , fire , lightning , meteorite , tornado , tsunami , thunderstorm , starvation , revolt , robbers , pirates , disease , conflagration , Disaster-Gauge-* , Disaster-Icon-Background(-Active) Pennants pennant-<colour> (12) Dice dice-icon-<building>-red (barracks, castle, church, cottage, house, sorcerer-tower) Technology slots Technology-Slot-Background- and Technology-Slot-Foreground- + Hovered , Learnable , Learnt , Locked Buttons and frames Button-1-* , Button-2-* ( Disabled , Hovered , Pressed , Ready ), Ornament-1..5 , Rounded_Rect_10px , Scroll-Handle , Knob , Checkmark , Background-3 , Background-4 , Event-Banner Rules screens rules-building-1..4 , rules-units-1..2 , rules-upgrades-1 , rules-disasters-1 , rules-game-phases-1..4 , rules-how-to-play-1..3 , rules-title-banner Menu settings , host , exit , ai , steam , discord , about , key , logo-title , back-to-menu , scoreboard , scoreboard-button The complete list can be printed from a mod with Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<Sprite>() (name, texture.name , size); sprites in an atlas appear twice, once as repacked and once with the atlas texture. Naming a new civilization's assets Follow the same pattern so the assets sort and read like the game's: Castle Atlantis for a prefab, building-icon-castle-atlantis-red for a sprite. The game never reads the names of a mod civilization's assets (the lookups are by type), so the names are only for you and for tools like the dump. What a complete skin needs Part Count Notes Building prefabs up to 24 Anything missing falls back to Europe. Building icons 12 per building One per player colour, in colour order. Unit prefabs up to 10 Same fallback. Unit icons 12 per unit Same. Ship prefab 1 Nature hubs 3 per biome Which biome a mod civilization uses is set by the civilization it looks like ( skinsLike ).

docs.text: Civilizations in the game code The game has five civilizations, the enum DiceKingdoms.Interface.Civilization : Value Name Biome it uses 0 EUROPE PLAINS 1 MIDDLE_EAST DESERT 2 VIKING SNOW 3 ANCIENT MEDITERRANEAN 4 MAYA JUNGLE The civilization is almost not a gameplay concept: it chooses how a player looks , which tech tree the player gets , which AI build orders an AI uses and what the civilization is called . Each civilization has its own models for buildings, units, ships and nature, but the building and unit types , their stats and costs, and the technologies themselves are the same for everybody. This page lists every place where the number matters and what that place does with a number it does not know, which is what a mod civilization has to deal with. Making a civilization is the practical guide. Where the number is used Where What it does With an unknown number PlayerSkins.Clone() Calls the constructor with the real number ( Rules.OnEnable clones the lobby's skins when the Rules screen opens). Throws the same exception when the Rules screen opens, which breaks it. PlayerSkins constructor and Civilization setter Stores the number and derives the biome with a switch over 0..4 (the table above). Throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException ( Parameter name: civilization ). PlayerSkins.Get{Building,Unit,Nature,InnerCliff}...Prefab , GetShipVisualPrefab Ask the skin registry for the replacement of a default prefab for this civilization (see below). Finds nothing and silently returns the default (European) prefab. PlayerSkinsSerialization Sends the civilization over the network as one byte ( WritePlayerSkins writes a byte, ReadPlayerSkins and the network variable's stream reader read an sbyte ) and builds PlayerSkins from it. Throws in the constructor; the receiving game freezes. A number above 127 arrives as another number. Technologies.TechTree(civilization) First(...) over the game's list of TechTree assets, matching TechTree.civilization . The compiler inlined it into Statistics.get_TechTree and Statistics.IsTechnologyLearnable , so those throw too. Throws InvalidOperationException: Sequence contains no matching element ; TechTreeInterface.Update asks every frame, so the log floods and the research window is dead. AIPlay.SampleBuildOrder(random, civilization, strategies) Keeps the build orders written for exactly that civilization. Throws No build order matching civilization=N, strategies=... . Player.NextCivilization The castle click on the match-start screen: steps through Player.Inventory.UnlockedCivilizations (Steam inventory) and wraps around. Only unlocked civilizations are ever offered. ITextElement.Localized with the key civilization.{value}.name The civilization's name in the text table. A missing-translation text. Rules window The civilization drop-down lists Enum.GetValues(typeof(Civilization)) . Not listed; a mod has to append its entries (see Rules and civilizations ). Not used by gameplay: IconRenderer has one sprite atlas per civilization for buildings and units (an icon-rendering tool, with buildingIconsFolder and testFolder fields; the icons in the game come from the prefabs, below), and IslandGrid.testCivilization , TestCombat.attackCivilization/defenseCivilization and Player.TestInit are test code. Skins: what a civilization looks like PlayerSkins is a small object (civilization, biome, a SkinRegistry , and caches). It hands out prefabs: Method Returns Original (default) prefab comes from GetBuildingVisualPrefab(BuildingType) BuildingVisual BuildingType.visualPrefab GetUnitVisualPrefab(Unit.Type) UnitVisual DefaultPrefabs.Unit(type) GetNatureVisualHubPrefab(NatureTile) NatureVisualHub DefaultPrefabs.Nature(tile) GetInnerCliffVisualHubPrefab(InnerCliff.Key) InnerCliffVisualHub DefaultPrefabs.InnerCliff(key) GetShipVisualPrefab() ShipVisual DefaultPrefabs.Ship Each call is SkinRegistry.GetSkinVariant(original, biome, civilization, variant) , which looks up a key of (original prefab, optional biome, optional civilization, variant text) in a dictionary built from the registry's entries list ( SkinRegistry.Awake runs OnValidate , which builds it) and returns the original when there is no entry . The player skins cache each result. So the five built-in civilizations are not code: they are entries of the skin registry that replace default prefabs by civilization, and a civilization with no entries looks European. Results are cached per PlayerSkins , so a skin change after a player has been drawn needs a new PlayerSkins object. The types a prefab needs (fields of the game's own components; names are from the IL2CPP dump): Prefab Component Main parts Building BuildingVisual visual and damagedVisual (the models), firesHolder , onlyEnableWhenActive , buildingTints (materials that take the player colour), hitSound , fireSound , placeParticlesPrefab , damageParticles , remainsParticles , icons Unit UnitVisual unitType , animator (parameters Move, Attack, AttackSpeed, Run), particlesParryPrefab , particlesDiePrefab , particlesConvertPrefab , buildingTints , icons , sounds (parry, die, walk, convert) Ship ShipVisual unitVisualsHolder (soldiers stand on it), animator (parameters Deploy, Sand, Move), particles , hideParent , colliders , sounds (sail, deploy) Nature NatureVisualHub natureTile and a list of NatureVisual children; SampleVisual(random) picks one Cliff InnerCliffVisualHub key and a list of transforms, one picked at random The tile kinds and unit kinds: BuildingTypeName (24): ARCHERY_RANGE, BARRACKS, CASTLE, CATHEDRAL, CHURCH, COTTAGE, DOCK, FARM, GUARD_TOWER, GUARD_TOWER_UP, HOSPITAL, HOUSE, LUMBER_CAMP, MARKET, SORCERER_TOWER, STONE_QUARRY, STORAGE, UNIVERSITY, WALL, WINDMILL, WONDER, FISHING_SHIP, LIGHTHOUSE, LAND_CAMP Unit.Type (10): ARCHER, BOURGEOIS, GENERAL, KING, PEASANT, PRIEST, SOLDIER, SORCERER, TEMPLAR, WARLOCK NatureTile (6): TREE, ROCK, SCORCHED_EARTH, LAVA, FLOWER, FISH Icons. BuildingVisual.Icon(PlayerColor) and UnitVisual.Icon(PlayerColor) return icons[color.Index] : one sprite per player colour , so a model with its own icon needs a full set. Technologies draw their icon with Technology.Icon(PlayerSkins, PlayerColor) : the "unlock building" technologies use the icon of the building in the player's skin (so a civilization's own model changes the research icon too), every other technology ( IconTechnology ) has one fixed icon sprite. Biome. The biome (ground, trees, rocks) is chosen with the civilization in PlayerSkins and cannot be set separately : a mod civilization takes the biome of the built-in civilization it is built "like". There is no way to give it a sixth biome through the skins alone. Tech trees Technologies (one asset) holds the 22 shared technologies ; Technology is abstract ( name , cost , Icon , OnLearn ). A technology never belongs to a tree. TechnologyName : ADDITIONAL_ROLL 0, DOUBLE_CLEAN_TILE 1, UPGRADE_GUARD_TOWER 2, TEMPLARS 3, WARLOCKS 4, UNLOCK_STORAGE 5, UNLOCK_LUMBER_CAMP 6, UNLOCK_STONE_QUARRY 7, UNLOCK_GUARD_TOWER 8, UNLOCK_SORCERER_TOWER 9, UNLOCK_HOSPITAL 10, UNLOCK_MARKET 11, UNLOCK_CATHEDRAL 12, UNLOCK_WINDMILL 13, UNLOCK_ARCHERY_RANGE 14, UNLOCK_WONDER 15, UNLOCK_FISHING_SHIP 16, UNLOCK_LIGHTHOUSE 17, UNLOCK_LAND_CAMP 18, RITUALS 19, SHIP_HOLD_OPTIMIZATION 20, TRADE_EFFICIENCY 21. A TechTree asset ( civilization , slots ) chooses and arranges them. A Slot has a technology , a grid position ( int2 ) and links ( toTechnology , toSlot , fromPort , toPort ). The research window draws exactly these: slots as boxes, links as lines. Dependencies are the links. GetDependencies(technology) returns the technologies of the slots that link to it, and caches the answer in a dictionary ( OnValidate clears the cache). Learnable rule ( Statistics.IsTechnologyLearnable ): not already learnt; in the Steam demo only UNLOCK_STORAGE can be learnt; and either it has no dependencies or at least one dependency is learnt. Which tree applies is Statistics.TechTree , from Statistics.island.Skins.civilization . Technologies.TechTree(civilization) is the lookup that every tree request goes through (and is inlined into the two Statistics members above). AI build orders AIPlay loads 15 build orders (3 per built-in civilization: culture , wonder , military_macro ) from text embedded in the game , in a small format: civilization=VIKING weight=2 strategy=MILITARY name=military_macro [ technologies [ UNLOCK_FISHING_SHIP UNLOCK_ARCHERY_RANGE ... ] buildings [ house house church cot cot ... ] ] The civilization is a Civilization enum name, the strategy is WONDER or MILITARY , and buildings is the order in which the AI builds, written with short words (house, cot, church, farm, racks, dock, land, storage, mill, fish, guard, cat, university, market, lumber, quarry, archery, wonder, sorcerer; they read as HOUSE, COTTAGE, CHURCH, FARM, BARRACKS, DOCK, LAND_CAMP, STORAGE, WINDMILL, FISHING_SHIP, GUARD_TOWER, CATHEDRAL, UNIVERSITY, MARKET, LUMBER_CAMP, STONE_QUARRY, ARCHERY_RANGE, WONDER, SORCERER_TOWER). The text is a compiled-in constant, so a mod cannot add orders; a mod civilization's AI uses the orders of the civilization it is "like". Networking A player's PlayerSkins travels as one byte (the sender writes a byte, the receiver reads an sbyte and calls the constructor). So a civilization number must fit in a signed byte, and 0..4 are taken: mod civilizations get 5..127 (123 numbers). Both sides must know the number: a client that does not have the mod would throw in the constructor on receiving it. A mod therefore has to make sure every lobby member has a civilization before it can be picked (for example by publishing its civilizations in the Steam lobby member data, offering the castle click only civilizations everybody has, and moving a player off a civilization somebody lacks). Localization Text goes through Unity Localization. StructuredTextStaticReferences.instance has the localizationSettings and the string table ( localizationStringTable ); ITextElement.Localized.Render looks a key up there. The civilization name key is string.Format("civilization.{0}.name", civilization) : civilization.EUROPE.name for a built-in one and civilization.14.name for a mod one (a boxed enum without a name prints its number). The table of a language is created when the language loads, so an entry has to be added to the table of the language in use and again when the language changes.

docs.text: Combat Units Unit.Type : ARCHER 0, BOURGEOIS 1, GENERAL 2, KING 3, PEASANT 4, PRIEST 5, SOLDIER 6, SORCERER 7, TEMPLAR 8, WARLOCK 9. Unit.Family : INHABITANT 0, SOLDIER_MELEE 1, SOLDIER_RANGED 2. Soldiers are the "military" resource. UnDeployedUnits = stored military − DeployedUnits . Inhabitants defend their own building ( BuildingTypeHousing.unitType : Castle → King, Cottage → Peasant, Church → Priest, House → Bourgeois, Barracks → General, Sorcerer Tower → Sorcerer). Units have no hit points. A hit that is not parried or blocked kills. UnitStats (times in combat ticks of 0.1 s): Unit Attack period Attack delay Aggro distance Parry Block arrow Ranged Kill reward pool Archer 9 7 6 1/2 – range 6, archer arrow, miss 1/5 – Bourgeois 8 4 256 1/5 – – hammer, stone General 6 3 256 4/5 4/5 – gold, military King 4 2 256 4/5 4/5 – gold, hammer Peasant 12 6 256 1/6 – – food, wood Priest 15 6 256 1/5 – – (converts) culture Soldier 6 3 6 2/3 – – – Sorcerer 10 4 184 1/3 – range 6, fireball, miss 1/2 disaster Templar 6 3 6 3/4 2/3 – – Warlock 9 3 6 1/2 – range 6, fireball, miss 1/5 – Aggro distance 256 = any enemy on the island. Ranges are in combat cells: the combat grid is finer than the island grid ( CombatGrid.FromIsland / ToIsland ), the Rules screen shows range 6 as "3 tiles". Planning an attack CombatData.PlanAttack(AttackPlan) ( 0x62E8E0 ) → PlanAttackRPC . AttackPlan = player, shipPosition (where the ship was dropped), target (building id), unitCounts per family, sourceDock . The plan is silently ignored if: the units sum to more than UnDeployedUnits ; the target player is on the same team (you cannot attack yourself or a teammate); a family with count > 0 is not unlocked; the dock is not in AvailableDocks . The dock is then removed from the list: one attack per dock per turn . DeployedUnits grows by the unit count. Not checked here: the ship capacity and the family cap. Those are enforced only by the attack UI and the AI, so a modified client could send more. Ship capacity Statistics.ShipCapacity = 8 × (1 + Ship Hold Optimization factor) = 8, or 16 with the technology. Family cap CombatPhase.FamilyUnitCap ( 0x63FA80 ): melee 999; other families 8 × the number of buildings of that family (8 ranged units per Archery Range). Templars replace Soldiers, Warlocks replace Archers ( SoldierFamilyUnitType : base Soldier / Archer, replaced by a learnt ReplaceSoldiers technology), for attackers and defenders. Deployments CombatPhase.ApplyChanges ( 0x63D870 ) builds the deployments for every island ( CreateDeployments 0x63E280 ), then the server prepares a combat for each island. The phase ends when every island reported its fight finished. Attacks: All plans of all players are shuffled with the match random generator; the order decides who gets the better landing spot. For each plan the target's shore tiles are tried nearest first to where the ship was dropped ( Deployment.AttackDeployment 0x643680 ). If none works, the attack is dropped : no ship sails, nothing is lost, and those soldiers defend at home this turn (confirmed in game). Soldiers sent on an attack do not defend their own island . Landing ( Deployment.Ship.BestDebarkTransform 0x64CF60 ): the ship needs a free 2×3 spot of water (sand allowed at the two front corners), not taken by another ship, in one of the 4 orientations, whose landing tile is in the same connected land area as the target building (or is a tile of it). Walls or buildings that cut the target off from every reachable shore make the attack impossible. 8 landing cells per ship; more soldiers come off in waves. Defenders: d = min(stored military − units sent away, DefLimit) ( DefLimit 999; developer command deflimit ). Garrison buildings (Castle, Barracks, Archery Range) get them, ranged first : n = min(d, family cap) per family, split evenly over that family's buildings. Example: 20 military, 1 Archery Range, Castle + 1 Barracks → 8 archers at the range, 12 melee split 6/6. Every active housing building also gets its inhabitants as defenders. An island only gets a fight if somebody attacks it; its own defence deployments alone do not start one. The simulation CombatGrid runs a deterministic, tick-based fight on every client : the server sends the deployment list, every machine simulates it with software floats ( sfloat ), grid positions, a Burst pathfinding job and seeded randomness. CombatGrid.Hash() is logged every 100 ticks ( Turn {0} - Island {1} - Tick {2} - Hash {3:x8} ) to catch desyncs. One tick = 0.1 s ( TICK_FREQUENCY 10). The fight stops at 3000 ticks (5 minutes) or after the grid was idle for more than 9 ticks. It starts after clamp(5 s − time since the phase sync, 0, 5 s) . SimulationStep ( 0x636E10 ), one tick: Take pathfinding results. Step every unit, deployment (landing), tower and projectile. Resolve the unit hits of this tick in random order: the target's parry roll, else it dies . Each death: the dead unit's owner loses 1 military ; if the killer is an enemy, the killer's owner gets +1 of a random resource from the dead unit's kill reward pool . Conversions (Priests): the old owner loses 1 military, the new owner gains 1, and the unit changes sides. Building hits: HP −= damage. Each destroyed building: if the attacker is not the island's owner, the attacker gets the building's pillage reward ; the building is removed and leaves remains. Units States: idle, moving, attacking. A hit lands at enterTick + attackDelay . Targets ( FindTarget 0x631D10 ): an enemy within 2 tiles always wins; else a defender within aggro distance; else (attackers) the nearest standing tile of the target building , or, once it is gone, a free exit tile on the ship. Defenders and inhabitants always go for the nearest enemy. An idle unit attacks anything enemy next to it ( AttackAnyOrIdle ): attackers also hit other enemy buildings they stand next to. Priests do not hit: they convert the unit on the target tile (only soldiers convert). Melee on a building tile : hits the building when no unit stands there, or with a 25 % roll when one does ( BUILDING_PROTECT_UNIT_CHANCE_PERCENT ). Melee damage to buildings is 1 , or 2 on a Wall when the attacker stands on its landing area. A hit on a Wall also damages every Wall directly next to it (one step, not a chain), so wall lines take damage in groups. Projectiles and towers Projectile Building damage Flight time (ticks, d = distance in tiles) Tower arrow 0 d × 20 / 100 + 5 Archer arrow 1 d × 50 / 100 + 1 Fireball (Sorcerer, Warlock) 8 d + 1 When a projectile lands: building tile → hits the building (no unit there, or the 25 % roll); else a unit on the tile: fireball kills , an arrow kills unless the unit's block roll succeeds. Arrow and fireball deaths do not use the parry roll. There is no team check where a projectile lands: allies and the defender's own buildings can be hit. Defenders' fireballs can destroy their own buildings (no pillage reward then). Miss : the shooter's miss roll moves the landing tile one tile in a random direction; the projectile still lands and hits what is there. Shooters aim where the target will be. Towers (Castle, Guard Tower, Guard Tower Up, Lighthouse): every tick the cooldown counts down; at 0 the tower picks among enemy units in range with score = random(0..255) − distance² (close units strongly preferred), shoots with its own miss roll, and waits period − 4 + random(0..8) ticks. Tower Range Period (ticks) Castle 60 30 Guard Tower 30 20 Guard Tower Up 45 13 Lighthouse 15 10 Parry, block and miss rolls (PRD) Parry, arrow block, ranged miss and tower miss use PseudoRandom ( Sample 0x64C790 ), like Dota's pseudo-random distribution: the chance drops after a success and rises after a failure, always pulled back toward the base value, so long streaks are rarer than with a plain random roll. next = 0.9 × f(next) + 0.1 × base f = Decrease(next) after a success, Increase(next) after a failure Decrease(x) = 1 − (1 − x) × exp(5 × x² × (1 − x)²) Increase(x) = 1 − Decrease(1 − x) = x × exp(5 × x² × (1 − x)²) Example: Decrease(0.5) = 0.317, Increase(0.5) = 0.683. End of a fight A fight normally ends when all attackers are dead or the target's Castle burns. Surviving attackers then walk back to their exit tiles and Deployment.Leave(survivors) sails them home. CombatGrid.End() ( 0x631C40 ) calls Leave with an empty list for deployments that did not leave yet (only visual). Soldiers are only lost by dying (−1 military each) or being converted; the fight ending loses nobody (confirmed in game). Power PowerConstants gives each unit type and the Castle, Guard Tower, Guard Tower Up and Wall a power value (Warlock 3, Templar 2, Sorcerer 2, Guard Tower Up 16, Guard Tower 8, Castle 4, …). AttackPower(island) / DefensePower(island) are shown in the player list and used by the AI . Developer helpers deflimit limits the number of defenders; MiscCommands.DebugAttack shows attack debug info. See Developer console .

docs.text: Unit.Type : ARCHER 0, BOURGEOIS 1, GENERAL 2, KING 3, PEASANT 4, PRIEST 5, SOLDIER 6, SORCERER 7, TEMPLAR 8, WARLOCK 9. Unit.Family : INHABITANT 0, SOLDIER_MELEE 1, SOLDIER_RANGED 2. Soldiers are the "military" resource. UnDeployedUnits = stored military − DeployedUnits . Inhabitants defend their own building ( BuildingTypeHousing.unitType : Castle → King, Cottage → Peasant, Church → Priest, House → Bourgeois, Barracks → General, Sorcerer Tower → Sorcerer). Units have no hit points. A hit that is not parried or blocked kills. UnitStats (times in combat ticks of 0.1 s): Unit Attack period Attack delay Aggro distance Parry Block arrow Ranged Kill reward pool Archer 9 7 6 1/2 – range 6, archer arrow, miss 1/5 – Bourgeois 8 4 256 1/5 – – hammer, stone General 6 3 256 4/5 4/5 – gold, military King 4 2 256 4/5 4/5 – gold, hammer Peasant 12 6 256 1/6 – – food, wood Priest 15 6 256 1/5 – – (converts) culture Soldier 6 3 6 2/3 – – – Sorcerer 10 4 184 1/3 – range 6, fireball, miss 1/2 disaster Templar 6 3 6 3/4 2/3 – – Warlock 9 3 6 1/2 – range 6, fireball, miss 1/5 – Aggro distance 256 = any enemy on the island. Ranges are in combat cells: the combat grid is finer than the island grid ( CombatGrid.FromIsland / ToIsland ), the Rules screen shows range 6 as "3 tiles".
docs.title: Units

docs.text: CombatData.PlanAttack(AttackPlan) ( 0x62E8E0 ) → PlanAttackRPC . AttackPlan = player, shipPosition (where the ship was dropped), target (building id), unitCounts per family, sourceDock . The plan is silently ignored if: the units sum to more than UnDeployedUnits ; the target player is on the same team (you cannot attack yourself or a teammate); a family with count > 0 is not unlocked; the dock is not in AvailableDocks . The dock is then removed from the list: one attack per dock per turn . DeployedUnits grows by the unit count. Not checked here: the ship capacity and the family cap. Those are enforced only by the attack UI and the AI, so a modified client could send more. Ship capacity Statistics.ShipCapacity = 8 × (1 + Ship Hold Optimization factor) = 8, or 16 with the technology. Family cap CombatPhase.FamilyUnitCap ( 0x63FA80 ): melee 999; other families 8 × the number of buildings of that family (8 ranged units per Archery Range). Templars replace Soldiers, Warlocks replace Archers ( SoldierFamilyUnitType : base Soldier / Archer, replaced by a learnt ReplaceSoldiers technology), for attackers and defenders.
docs.title: Planning an attack

docs.text: CombatPhase.ApplyChanges ( 0x63D870 ) builds the deployments for every island ( CreateDeployments 0x63E280 ), then the server prepares a combat for each island. The phase ends when every island reported its fight finished. Attacks: All plans of all players are shuffled with the match random generator; the order decides who gets the better landing spot. For each plan the target's shore tiles are tried nearest first to where the ship was dropped ( Deployment.AttackDeployment 0x643680 ). If none works, the attack is dropped : no ship sails, nothing is lost, and those soldiers defend at home this turn (confirmed in game). Soldiers sent on an attack do not defend their own island . Landing ( Deployment.Ship.BestDebarkTransform 0x64CF60 ): the ship needs a free 2×3 spot of water (sand allowed at the two front corners), not taken by another ship, in one of the 4 orientations, whose landing tile is in the same connected land area as the target building (or is a tile of it). Walls or buildings that cut the target off from every reachable shore make the attack impossible. 8 landing cells per ship; more soldiers come off in waves. Defenders: d = min(stored military − units sent away, DefLimit) ( DefLimit 999; developer command deflimit ). Garrison buildings (Castle, Barracks, Archery Range) get them, ranged first : n = min(d, family cap) per family, split evenly over that family's buildings. Example: 20 military, 1 Archery Range, Castle + 1 Barracks → 8 archers at the range, 12 melee split 6/6. Every active housing building also gets its inhabitants as defenders. An island only gets a fight if somebody attacks it; its own defence deployments alone do not start one.
docs.title: Deployments

docs.text: CombatGrid runs a deterministic, tick-based fight on every client : the server sends the deployment list, every machine simulates it with software floats ( sfloat ), grid positions, a Burst pathfinding job and seeded randomness. CombatGrid.Hash() is logged every 100 ticks ( Turn {0} - Island {1} - Tick {2} - Hash {3:x8} ) to catch desyncs. One tick = 0.1 s ( TICK_FREQUENCY 10). The fight stops at 3000 ticks (5 minutes) or after the grid was idle for more than 9 ticks. It starts after clamp(5 s − time since the phase sync, 0, 5 s) . SimulationStep ( 0x636E10 ), one tick: Take pathfinding results. Step every unit, deployment (landing), tower and projectile. Resolve the unit hits of this tick in random order: the target's parry roll, else it dies . Each death: the dead unit's owner loses 1 military ; if the killer is an enemy, the killer's owner gets +1 of a random resource from the dead unit's kill reward pool . Conversions (Priests): the old owner loses 1 military, the new owner gains 1, and the unit changes sides. Building hits: HP −= damage. Each destroyed building: if the attacker is not the island's owner, the attacker gets the building's pillage reward ; the building is removed and leaves remains.
docs.title: The simulation

docs.text: States: idle, moving, attacking. A hit lands at enterTick + attackDelay . Targets ( FindTarget 0x631D10 ): an enemy within 2 tiles always wins; else a defender within aggro distance; else (attackers) the nearest standing tile of the target building , or, once it is gone, a free exit tile on the ship. Defenders and inhabitants always go for the nearest enemy. An idle unit attacks anything enemy next to it ( AttackAnyOrIdle ): attackers also hit other enemy buildings they stand next to. Priests do not hit: they convert the unit on the target tile (only soldiers convert). Melee on a building tile : hits the building when no unit stands there, or with a 25 % roll when one does ( BUILDING_PROTECT_UNIT_CHANCE_PERCENT ). Melee damage to buildings is 1 , or 2 on a Wall when the attacker stands on its landing area. A hit on a Wall also damages every Wall directly next to it (one step, not a chain), so wall lines take damage in groups.

docs.text: Projectile Building damage Flight time (ticks, d = distance in tiles) Tower arrow 0 d × 20 / 100 + 5 Archer arrow 1 d × 50 / 100 + 1 Fireball (Sorcerer, Warlock) 8 d + 1 When a projectile lands: building tile → hits the building (no unit there, or the 25 % roll); else a unit on the tile: fireball kills , an arrow kills unless the unit's block roll succeeds. Arrow and fireball deaths do not use the parry roll. There is no team check where a projectile lands: allies and the defender's own buildings can be hit. docs.text: Developer console and debug keys The game ships CommandTerminal ( Terminal : MonoBehaviour , commands registered with [RegisterCommand] ). The commands are in DiceKingdoms.Meta.Cheats and MiscCommands . When cheats work Cheats.get_Available ( 0x52A840 ): Available = Cheats.gameState != null && gameState.players.Count(p => !p.IsAI) < 2 So the console commands work in a match with at most one human (you plus any number of AIs). Not in the main menu, not with two or more humans. There is no developer-build, Steam-id or setting check. CheckAvailable ( 0x528D40 ) logs "Cheats unavailable." otherwise. Forcing get_Available / CheckAvailable to return true unlocks them everywhere. Each command has a Front… handler (parses the arguments) and a Command… handler; both only write a field of the local Cheats object ( defLimit 0x30 , enabledDisasters 0x34 , forcedDisaster 0x38 , rich 0x40 , speedFactor 0x44 ), which the game logic then reads. There is no network message: it works match-wide only because the single human is the host. Commands Command Effect deflimit <n> limits the number of defenders ( Cheats.DefLimit , default 999) disasters <bool> disasters on / off forcedisaster <name> the chosen disaster hits the island itself (used in DisastersPhase.RandomOccurrences ) learnall learns every technology loadisland loads an island from the clipboard ( island code ) rich <bool> unlimited resources: storage is refilled to capacity continuously speed <factor> multiplies time ( Cheats.NetworkTime ) timer <bool> phase timer on / off cinematic / freecam ( MiscCommands ) smooth camera and anonymous players (colour names instead of Steam names); free camera also ignores the disaster camera lock debug build / attack / lobbies ( MiscCommands ) debug output (every build action logged, AI attack scoring, lobby info) net order prints the networked object order save island copies your island code to the clipboard ( IslandGrid.SaveIslandToClipboard ) Keys Key What F1 toggle the developer console Shift+F1 console in full-size mode F2 performance monitor (Tayx Graphy) on / off Ctrl+F3 Graphy: next display mode (also counts as F3) F3 hide / show the whole HUD; hiding it also hides and locks the mouse cursor Tab scoreboard R / T rotate / mirror the building being placed Shift keep placing Shift / Ctrl + send arrow send 5 / 10 resources instead of 1 (scoreboard) Key bindings (except the debug keys) can be changed in the settings; see Game UI .
