docs.text: Disasters Data The Disasters asset holds one object of each disaster class, in this order ( Values , index 0..12): starvation, robbers, disease, lightning, fire, thunderstorm, revolt, tornado, plague, satanism, pirates, tsunami, meteorite. Base class Disaster : name 0x10 , icon 0x18 , affectedOthers 0x20 , threshold 0x24 . # Disaster Threshold (disaster points) Hits Parameters 0 Starvation −1 (every turn) self – 1 Robbers 1 1 other player losable: food, wood, stone 2 Disease 2 self 50 % of candidates 3 Lightning 3 1 other player 2 tiles 4 Fire 4 self – 5 Thunderstorm 5 1 other player 5 tiles 6 Revolt 6 self 50 % of military lost 7 Tornado 7 2 other players – 8 Plague 8 self 50 % of candidates 9 Satanism 9 2 other players – 10 Pirates 10 self losable: wood, stone, gold; 50 % lost 11 Tsunami 11 all other players radius 5, start distance 28, 2550 ms to impact 12 Meteorite 12 self radius 4; see Meteorites Which disaster happens DisastersPhase.RandomOccurrences ( 0x646940 ), for every island: d = the island's stored disaster points . idx = FindLastIndex(Values, v => v.threshold >= 0 && v.threshold <= d) . The thresholds go up in order, so only one disaster per island happens: the strongest one whose threshold was reached. None if d is 0. Normally one occurrence. With the lobby option Multi-meteor and the meteorite: d − 12 + 1 meteors (every point over 12 adds one). Targets: the developer command forcedisaster makes the chosen disaster hit the island itself; affectedOthers < 1 : it hits the island that caused it; otherwise the other islands whose owner is on another team (free-for-all: every other player) and not defeated are shuffled with the match random generator, and the first affectedOthers become targets. Teammates and defeated players are never targeted. Each DisasterOccurrence(source, target, disaster, seed) gets its own seed from the match random generator, so every client plays it the same way. Then: Starvation is always added for every island (source = target = self), after its normal disaster. After all disasters ran, every island's disaster points are reset to 0. ExecuteOccurrencesRPC sends the list to all clients; each DisasterOccurrence.Execute(GameState) is a coroutine of delays. Affected buildings Building.Active is simply affectedByDisaster == null ( 0x5F15A0 ). An affected building (hungry, sick, …) does not roll its die and does not count as active population for that turn. The building tints (hungry / sick / burnt / died in combat) show the state. Effects Disaster Effect Starvation (food upkeep) needed = number of active housing buildings (Castle, Cottage, House, Church, Barracks, Sorcerer Tower); each eats 1 food ; min(needed, stored food) is removed. For every missing food one random active housing building becomes hungry . Robbers Picks a random resource among food / wood / stone that the target has: the target loses 1, the sender gains 1 . Disease Candidates = buildings that can get sick and touch a building that can contaminate ; half of them (rounded down) become sick for the turn. Lightning A random free grass tile and a connected blob of up to 2 free tiles get scorched earth ( IslandGrid.StormDisaster ). Never hits buildings; scorched earth blocks building until it is cleaned. Fire One random burnable building on your island is destroyed. Thunderstorm Like Lightning with 5 tiles. Revolt You lose half your stored military (rounded down): 1 soldier → 0 lost, 3 → 1. Tornado Like Fire, on each target island. Plague Like Disease, but every building that can get sick is a candidate (no contaminating neighbour needed); Hospitals still protect. Satanism A random house is replaced by a Sorcerer Tower (inside the old tiles, full HP), which then produces more disaster points. Pirates You lose half (rounded down) of your wood, stone and gold. Nobody receives them. Tsunami See below. Meteorite Crater of radius 4, scorched earth and lava, with castle protection: Meteorites . Burnable = not a fortification and not a Castle. Only the Wall is a fortification, so Fire and Tornado can destroy anything except Walls and Castles (Guard Towers included). Can get sick ( IslandGrid.CanGetSick 0x613D70 ): housing, producers except the Farm, technology buildings, the Market; but not if a Hospital touches it or touches a non-wall neighbour of it (the Hospital protects its neighbours and their neighbours; walls block it). Can contaminate : not a wall, not a Farm, not a Hospital, and no Hospital next to it. Tsunami Impact point ( GetTsunamiImpact 0x615C00 ): from a random land tile, a 3-wide ray toward the island centre; the first land tile with water next to it is the impact. Tiles ( GetTsunamiTiles 0x625890 ): land tiles in rings up to radius 5 around the impact with a clear straight line from it. The line may not cross a hill edge ( INNER_CLIFF ), so tiles behind a hill are safe (confirmed in game). Each tile ( IslandGrid.TsunamiDisaster 0x61C970 ): any building on it is removed (there is no Castle exception: a tsunami touching one tile of a Castle burns the whole Castle; confirmed in game), then grass, sand, meteorite ground and piers become water and lose their nature. Water rocks and hill edges stay. A Land Camp can turn the water back into land. Playback and the camera DisastersPhase.ExecuteOccurrences ( 0x645900 ) runs on every client and builds one sequence: Small disasters (everything except tornado, tsunami and meteorite): the camera flies to your own island (0.8 s) and is locked; they all play at the same time on all islands. Big disasters (tornado, tsunami, meteorite), grouped by target island: for each, the camera flies to that island (0.8 s, locked), waits 0.5 s, plays them one after another, then waits 1 s. The camera flies back to your island (0.5 s) and is released. If you are defeated, it is just released where it is. Each client then acknowledges the end; the server moves on when every client has. While CameraMovement.focus has a value, CameraMovement.Update zeroes all camera input, so the player cannot move the camera during the disaster animations . The developer console's free camera ( MiscCommands.FreeCam ) skips the focus. A mod that wants free camera control can clear cameraMovement.focus (set it to null ) every frame during this phase; it is display only and does not affect sync. The visual effects of each disaster are listed in Rendering .

docs.text: Game data Values read from the game's assets (game version 1.0.4). Unit stats are on Combat , die faces on Harvest , disasters on Disasters , AI values on AI . Match Phase Time limit (timer FAST) Start ("Settle") 60 s Harvest 40 s (+5 s sync) Disasters none Build 70 s Combat 35 s Win none Timer SLOW = ×1.5, UNLIMITED = no limit; solo games are always UNLIMITED. Lobby defaults: timer FAST, multi-meteor off, teams off, wonder victory on. Start resources: 3 food, 3 wood, 2 stone, 4 hammers, 8 culture . Build phase prices: tool cost (clean a tile, repair, burn) 1 hammer ; repair restores 60 HP. Market: 1 gold → 2 food, 1 wood, 1 stone, 1 military or 1 hammer (×2 with Trade Efficiency). die; defender King; garrison Wall (18) 1 1 50 1 stone, 1 hammer – 1 stone – placed in bulk of 10; fortification Farm (7) 8 1 15 1 wood, 1 hammer – – 1 food 1 food per harvest Cottage (5) 2 1 10 2 wood, 1 hammer – 2 food, 1 wood, 1 hammer 1 wood die; docs.text: Harvest and dice Who rolls dice HarvestData.Roll ( 0x649BC0 ): only buildings whose type is BuildingTypeHousing (or its subclass BuildingTypeCastle ) roll, and only while Building.Active (a hungry or sick building is inactive). BuildingTypeHousing field Offset Meaning possibleYields 0xE8 ResourceAmount[] , the faces of the die diceColor 0xF0 Color unitType 0x100 the inhabitant that defends this building in combat dicePrefab 0x108 Dice visual The result for one building is RandomExtensions.NextSample(possibleYields) : a uniform pick of one face, using the per-island random generator ( IslandGrid + 0xFC ). A missing, inactive or non-housing building gives ResourceAmount.ZERO . "Disaster" is one of the eight resources, so dice faces can give disaster points (see Disasters ). Die faces Building Faces Castle 2 food · 1 food, 1 hammer · 1 gold · 2 military · 1 food, 1 stone · 1 gold, 1 military, 1 disaster Cottage 4 food · 3 wood · 1 wood, 1 stone · 1 food, 2 hammer · 1 food, 1 stone · 1 wood, 1 hammer, 1 disaster Church 2 food · 1 wood, 1 stone · 1 food, 2 culture · 1 wood, 2 culture · 1 stone, 2 culture · 3 culture, 1 disaster House 3 stone · 3 hammer · 1 stone, 1 gold · 1 wood, 1 gold · 1 gold, 1 culture · 1 stone, 1 hammer, 1 disaster Barracks 1 wood, 2 military · 2 military · 3 military · 4 military · 1 gold, 1 military · 2 military, 1 disaster Sorcerer Tower 1 wood · 1 stone · 4 gold · 5 culture · 3 disaster · 4 disaster Every die except the Sorcerer Tower's has exactly one face with 1 disaster point; the Sorcerer Tower has two faces with 3 and 4. Re-rolls HarvestData.Reset ( 0x649520 ): BASE_RE_ROLLS = 2 ; TotalReRolls = 2 + the sum of AddRollTechnology.value over learnt technologies (technology ADDITIONAL_ROLL , +1). The server makes the first roll. The player picks dice and calls ReRoll(Building.Id[]) → ReRollRPC ; the server rolls them again and broadcasts RollResultsRPC(results, reRollsRemaining) . Dice are animated client-side; the result is decided on the server before the animation (see Rendering ). Total yield HarvestData.ComputeTotalYields ( 0x648530 ) builds TotalYields from scratch: every dice result of this harvest; plus BuildingTypeProducer.Yield(building, island) of every active producer building (passive income, below); Rituals: for every other island whose owner is not on my team (in free-for-all: every other player) and who has learnt Rituals, each active Sorcerer Tower there adds skullPerSorcererTower (1) disaster point to my yield. In team mode Rituals never hurts teammates. HarvestData.AddResources ( 0x648470 ) adds TotalYields to the island's Statistics with AddResource , capped at the storage capacity , then resets TotalYields . Passive producers Subclasses of BuildingTypeProducer implement Yield(Island, Building) : Class Formula Buildings BuildingTypeProducerFixed fixed yield ( 0xE8 ) Farm: 1 food BuildingTypeProducerNature ( 0x60B890 ) (neighbouring nature tiles / tilesNeeded ) × (2 if a Lighthouse covers it) Lumber Camp: wood per TREE; Stone Quarry: stone per ROCK; Fishing Ship: food per FISH BuildingTypeProducerAmplifier ( 0x60B300 ) count on island × amplifyFactor + count next to it × amplifyFactorProximityBonus Cathedral: 2 culture per Church on the island + 1 per adjacent Church; Windmill: 3 food per adjacent Farm BuildingTypeApplyModifierInRange applies BuildingModifier.DOUBLE_FISH to Fishing Ships within range 20 of a Lighthouse (it does not stack). BuildingTypeLandExtension (Land Camp) implements IBuildingTypeUpdateOnHarvest : each harvest it turns up to 24 water tiles within range 6 into land. Storage capacity Island.RecomputeStorageCapacities ( 0x61F270 ): the capacity is the sum of BuildingType.storageCapacity over all buildings on the island. Nothing else adds to it. Building Storage Castle 15 food, 10 wood, 10 stone, 999 gold, 999 hammers, 999 culture, 8 military, 999 disaster Storage 10 food, 20 wood, 20 stone Barracks, Archery Range 8 military each Gold, hammers, culture and disaster are only raised by more Castles; Storage buildings only raise food, wood and stone. The Storage research only unlocks the building. It is recomputed after every phase, so a building placed in the build phase raises the capacity at the end of that phase (confirmed in game). Statistics.SetCapacity → ResourceStorage.WithCapacity clamps every stored amount to the new capacity. That is why losing buildings throws away resources above the new capacity, and why burning the last Castle empties everything. Encrypted storage The resources are kept in Utility.AntiCheat.EncryptedStorage<ResourceStorage> inside Statistics : the 64 bytes of ResourceStorage XOR a random per-write key XOR a per-launch static key. A memory scanner will not find plain values. Mods do not need to decrypt anything: read Statistics.get_Storage (plain ResourceStorage ) and change resources with Statistics.AddResource / RemoveResource / SetCapacity . Food upkeep Each turn the Disasters phase charges 1 food per active housing building . Missing food makes random buildings hungry (inactive, so no dice next harvest).

docs.text: Interface behaviour How the in-match interface behaves. The visual building blocks (canvases, buttons, window art, settings rows, aspect ratios) are on Game UI . Who owns what Interface (one per match, GameState.@interface ) references the CameraMovement , Training , StartGame and the arrays requireStartGame / hideInterface . It holds GameState , Island (the local player's island; null for spectators) and Hidden , and has events used by the tutorial: OnBuild(BuildingType) , OnLearn(Technology) , OnPillage() , OnStarvation(...) . One phase interface per phase: StartInterface , HarvestInterface , BuildInterface , CombatInterface , WinInterface (disasters only have visuals). Base class PhaseInterface<TData, TIslandState> with Data , TurnPhase , GameState , Island , Owner , BannerDuration , virtual Enter() , abstract Sync() , optional PhaseBanner . TurnPhase.Enter enables the phase interface component on clients and calls its Enter() ; TurnPhase.Exit disables it. So a phase screen is only enabled during its phase: its OnEnable / OnDisable / Enter are the hook points for UI that belongs to one phase. Global alternatives: GameState.onEnterPhase , onSyncPhase , onStartGame , onEndGame . Interface.Update ( 0x5A6630 ): F3 toggles Hidden (every object in hideInterface is switched off: screenshot mode). The mouse cursor is hidden and locked while the camera is grabbed or the HUD is hidden, otherwise visible and confined to the window . Input Map Action Binding Camera Move WASD / arrow keys Camera Zoom mouse wheel Camera Grab Space or middle mouse Camera MouseMove mouse delta while grabbed Building Rotate / Mirror R / T Building Place, Select left mouse Building Cancel Esc or right mouse Building KeepPlacing Shift (hold) Interface Scoreboard / Chat Tab / Enter Bindings are physical key positions (layout independent). InputActionMaps (a ScriptableObject) has StartDisable(map) → DisableToken ; token.Stop() re-enables. A map is disabled while at least one token is active. The game uses it only for chat. Text fields in a mod window Get the asset with Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<InputActionMaps>()[0] and take StartDisable(Camera) and StartDisable(Building) tokens while your field has focus, then Stop() both. Otherwise WASD moves the camera and R / T rotate while typing. Camera CameraMovement : min height 4, max height 100, move speed 5, zoom speed 0.2, zoom smoothing 10, mouse move speed 0.002; pitch by height (0 → 0°, 4 → −30°, 25 → −55°, 100 → −90° straight down). The yaw is fixed at 45° (see Rendering ). focus ( Nullable<Focus> ): new Focus(IslandGrid grid, float duration = 0.5, bool stopAfterEnd = true) or Focus(float2 position, float radius, float endTime, bool stopAfterEnd) . To fly the camera to an island: cameraMovement.focus = new Il2CppSystem.Nullable<CameraMovement.Focus>(new CameraMovement.Focus(island.grid, 1f, true)) (confirmed in game). While focus has a value, all camera input is ignored ( UpdatePositionFocus zeroes it) until it arrives ( stopAfterEnd = true ) or is cleared. The disasters phase uses this to lock the camera ( Disasters ). The console's free camera skips the focus. FocusedIsland = the island nearest to the camera within 15 units. Clicking a player in the player list flies the camera to that island ( PlayerSummary.OnPointerClick ). Build phase tools BuildInterface owns BuildingPlacer (single buildings), BuildingBulkPlacer (walls: drag a path), CleanTileTool , BuildingSelector (click a building → repair / burn), MarketInterface , UniversityInterface , TechnologyInterface , ConfirmModal , DisasterGauge and AvailableActions (hint bar of usable keys). Flow: building button → BuildingPlacer.SetCurrentBuildingType(type) → left click → BuildInterface.OnPlace → BuildData.PlaceBuilding . With Shift held and still affordable the placer stays active. BuildInterface.Update refreshes the building buttons only when stored resources or the number of learnt technologies changed. Repair / burn are enabled when you can pay the tool cost and the building is on your island. Nothing filters the Castle ( Build phase ). TilePointer = the tile under the mouse (island, position, orientation, mirroring, footprint preview). Mouse cursor Utility.UI.CursorVariation (ScriptableObject): texture + hotSpot ; Use() = Cursor.SetCursor (hardware cursor). Utility.UI.CursorHelper keeps a priority stack of overrides: StartOverride(variation, priority) returns an Override (with a token); EndOverride(override) removes it. The highest priority is shown; when the list is empty the default cursor ( cursor-default.png , hotspot 1, 1) is used. Users: BaseButton hover (priority 10 ), HooverCursor component (0), clean-tile tool, building placers, combat planning (attack / ship, valid / invalid) (all 0). So a button hover always wins. Cursor assets: Hand (8, 1), Build (1, 16), Clean-Tile (1, 27), Attack / Attack-Invalid (1, 1), Ship / Ship-Invalid (5, 5). TileCursor / TileCursorPart are not the mouse cursor: they are the animated 3D tile highlights on the island. For your own UI: add HooverCursor , or call StartOverride with priority above 10 and always EndOverride on exit / disable. Text: StructuredText StructuredText is a list of ITextElement built from a C# interpolated string ( $"..." ); Render() gives the TextMeshPro string, + joins two. Each {hole} is converted by type: Value type Becomes ITextElement / StructuredText itself / its elements int number Resource resource icon ResourceAmount for each resource > 0: the icon repeated N times (N ≤ 3 and total < 6), else "N" + icon Color colour start (close with ITextElement.End.INSTANCE ) Player / Team coloured player name / team BuildingTypeHousing dice icon (BuildingType, Player) , (Unit.Type, Player) , (Technology, Player) building / unit / technology in that player's skin Disaster disaster string text, with tokens parsed Tokens inside strings (also inside localized texts): {a.N} (the N-th element argument), {b.<building type>} , {d.<disaster>} , {r.<resource>} (food, wood, stone, gold, hammer, culture, military, disaster), {o.<icon>} (hungry, scoreboard, research, question-mark, ship, population, clean-tile). Unknown tokens are dropped. In a C# interpolated string the token braces must be doubled: $"{player} got 5 {{r.gold}}" . Other elements: Localized(key, args) , OtherIcon (AI, CLEAN_TILE, DISCONNECTED, HOST, HUNGRY, POPULATION, QUESTION_MARK, RESEARCH, SHIP, ATTACK_POWER, SHIELD, SCOREBOARD). Tooltips, dialogs, game log, chat Tooltips: add HasToolTip to a UI object and set .text (a StructuredText ); shown after 0.4 s. Dialogs: ConfirmModal.OpenConfirm(icon, description, onCancel, onConfirm, dontShowAgainId) and OpenInformation(icon, description, onUnderstood, dontShowAgainId) : the game's own dialog, reusable. Game log: Log is networked. Log.AddMessage(StructuredText) works on the server only (a client just logs a warning); the entry syncs to every client, so a host-side mod can post messages everybody sees. Rows are visible 30 s and fade in 1 s. Chat ( ChatInterface ): Enter opens the field and disables the other input maps; sending calls Player.Local.Chat(text) (the host adds it to the log). While chat is open every chat and log row stays visible, and fades again 1 s after closing. Timer, Ready, banners Timer: turn number and ceil(time remaining) ( TimeRemaining while ACTIVE, TimeRemainingSync while SYNC; empty without a limit). The clock hand: Start / Harvest 0°, Disasters 90°, Build 180°, Combat 270°. A tick sound plays for each of the last 4 seconds ; a "waiting for you" sound plays once after 2 s when the others are ready and you are not. Ready button: click = TurnPhase.PhaseData(myIsland).Skip() . Clickable only while the phase is ACTIVE, after the 2 s banner, when you are not ready yet and the phase allows skipping. If the phase already considers you ready, it skips by itself. Phase banner: slides in from 1024 px above, leaves after 2 s ( disappearAfter , which is also BannerDuration ), switched off at 2.5 s. Changing disappearAfter also changes when Ready becomes clickable. Imminent victory warning: on every phase start (not the Win phase) WinPhase.CheckWin() is evaluated; if the predicted winner changed, or during every Build phase while a Wonder win is pending, the warning shows for 6 s and fades in the last 1 s. Counters (57 animated numbers) move toward their target at |target − value| × 2 + 10 per second. Screens Harvest ( HarvestInterface ): one Dice per housing building, a "keep" and a "re-roll" grid; clicking a die moves it. The face is decided by the game before the throw, so a mod that changes yields afterwards does not change the face shown. Combat planning ( CombatInterface ): a slider per unit family, the ship "ghost" ( shipPreview ) and ClosestValidDebarkTransform for the landing preview. No ghost on your own island. Scoreboard (Tab): win conditions (military: defeated / total; wonder: own vs best other, missing resources, win delay), ping, resources, population, technologies. Send-resource arrows : 1 per click, Shift 5, Ctrl 10, capped by what you have → BuildData.SendResources . Shown only in the Build phase, when you are not defeated, for other players (teammates only in team games), and only with an available Market (active, not placed this phase). Player list ( PlayerSummary ): attack / defence power, population, connection, disaster log; click = fly to that island. TechTreeInterface is data-driven ( TechTree , IsTechnologyLearnt/Learnable/DemoLocked , StoredResources , OnClickTechnology , then Populate() ) and can be reused for a mod's own tree. WinInterface : victory visual, Continue / Exit / Discord / Steam buttons, gold gained. StartInterface : placer + selector for the start buildings. Settings widgets SettingSetInterface.GenerateElements ( 0x54D2F0 ) builds the settings window by reflection over a SettingSet : an optional header ( settings.<set>.header.<key> ), then for every setting a row labelled settings.<set>.setting.<name> with a widget chosen by the setting's value type : bool → toggle, float → slider (range from the setting), enums ( FullScreenMode , Language , Quality , TimerSpeed ) and ScreenResolution → drop-down, input path → key rebinding (keyboard keys only), lobby code. An unknown type throws. So a new field of a supported type on a SettingSet appears in the game's own window (it needs the localization keys). HUD layout Positions in 1920×1080 reference units; off = inactive in the scene, switched on by code. docs.text: How the in-match interface behaves. The visual building blocks (canvases, buttons, window art, settings rows, aspect ratios) are on Game UI .

docs.text: Interface (one per match, GameState.@interface ) references the CameraMovement , Training , StartGame and the arrays requireStartGame / hideInterface . It holds GameState , Island (the local player's island; null for spectators) and Hidden , and has events used by the tutorial: OnBuild(BuildingType) , OnLearn(Technology) , OnPillage() , OnStarvation(...) . One phase interface per phase: StartInterface , HarvestInterface , BuildInterface , CombatInterface , WinInterface (disasters only have visuals). Base class PhaseInterface<TData, TIslandState> with Data , TurnPhase , GameState , Island , Owner , BannerDuration , virtual Enter() , abstract Sync() , optional PhaseBanner . TurnPhase.Enter enables the phase interface component on clients and calls its Enter() ; TurnPhase.Exit disables it. So a phase screen is only enabled during its phase: its OnEnable / OnDisable / Enter are the hook points for UI that belongs to one phase. Global alternatives: GameState.onEnterPhase , onSyncPhase , onStartGame , onEndGame . Interface.Update ( 0x5A6630 ): F3 toggles Hidden (every object in hideInterface is switched off: screenshot mode). The mouse cursor is hidden and locked while the camera is grabbed or the HUD is hidden, otherwise visible and confined to the window .
docs.title: Who owns what

docs.text: Map Action Binding Camera Move WASD / arrow keys Camera Zoom mouse wheel Camera Grab Space or middle mouse Camera MouseMove mouse delta while grabbed Building Rotate / Mirror R / T Building Place, Select left mouse Building Cancel Esc or right mouse Building KeepPlacing Shift (hold) Interface Scoreboard / Chat Tab / Enter Bindings are physical key positions (layout independent). InputActionMaps (a ScriptableObject) has StartDisable(map) → DisableToken ; token.Stop() re-enables. A map is disabled while at least one token is active. The game uses it only for chat. Text fields in a mod window Get the asset with Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll<InputActionMaps>()[0] and take StartDisable(Camera) and StartDisable(Building) tokens while your field has focus, then Stop() both. Otherwise WASD moves the camera and R / T rotate while typing.
docs.title: Input

docs.text: CameraMovement : min height 4, max height 100, move speed 5, zoom speed 0.2, zoom smoothing 10, mouse move speed 0.002; pitch by height (0 → 0°, 4 → −30°, 25 → −55°, 100 → −90° straight down). The yaw is fixed at 45° (see Rendering ). focus ( Nullable<Focus> ): new Focus(IslandGrid grid, float duration = 0.5, bool stopAfterEnd = true) or Focus(float2 position, float radius, float endTime, bool stopAfterEnd) . To fly the camera to an island: cameraMovement.focus = new Il2CppSystem.Nullable<CameraMovement.Focus>(new CameraMovement.Focus(island.grid, 1f, true)) (confirmed in game). While focus has a value, all camera input is ignored ( UpdatePositionFocus zeroes it) until it arrives ( stopAfterEnd = true ) or is cleared. The disasters phase uses this to lock the camera ( Disasters ). The console's free camera skips the focus. FocusedIsland = the island nearest to the camera within 15 units. Clicking a player in the player list flies the camera to that island ( PlayerSummary.OnPointerClick ).
docs.title: Camera

docs.text: BuildInterface owns BuildingPlacer (single buildings), BuildingBulkPlacer (walls: drag a path), CleanTileTool , BuildingSelector (click a building → repair / burn), MarketInterface , UniversityInterface , TechnologyInterface , ConfirmModal , DisasterGauge and AvailableActions (hint bar of usable keys). Flow: building button → BuildingPlacer.SetCurrentBuildingType(type) → left click → BuildInterface.OnPlace → BuildData.PlaceBuilding . With Shift held and still affordable the placer stays active. BuildInterface.Update refreshes the building buttons only when stored resources or the number of learnt technologies changed. Repair / burn are enabled when you can pay the tool cost and the building is on your island. Nothing filters the Castle ( Build phase ). TilePointer = the tile under the mouse (island, position, orientation, mirroring, footprint preview).
docs.title: Build phase tools

docs.text: Utility.UI.CursorVariation (ScriptableObject): texture + hotSpot ; Use() = Cursor.SetCursor (hardware cursor). Utility.UI.CursorHelper keeps a priority stack of overrides: StartOverride(variation, priority) returns an Override (with a token); EndOverride(override) removes it. The highest priority is shown; when the list is empty the default cursor ( cursor-default.png , hotspot 1, 1) is used. Users: BaseButton hover (priority 10 ), HooverCursor component (0), clean-tile tool, building placers, combat planning (attack / ship, valid / invalid) (all 0). So a button hover always wins. Cursor assets: Hand (8, 1), Build (1, 16), Clean-Tile (1, 27), Attack / Attack-Invalid (1, 1), Ship / Ship-Invalid (5, 5). TileCursor / TileCursorPart are not the mouse cursor: they are the animated 3D tile highlights on the island. For your own UI: add HooverCursor , or call StartOverride with priority above 10 and always EndOverride on exit / disable.
docs.title: Mouse cursor

docs.text: StructuredText is a list of ITextElement built from a C# interpolated string ( $"..." ); Render() gives the TextMeshPro string, + joins two. Each {hole} is converted by type: Value type Becomes ITextElement / StructuredText itself / its elements int number Resource resource icon ResourceAmount for each resource > 0: the icon repeated N times (N ≤ 3 and total < 6), else "N" + icon Color colour start (close with ITextElement.End.INSTANCE ) Player / Team coloured player name / team BuildingTypeHousing dice icon (BuildingType, Player) , (Unit.Type, Player) , (Technology, Player) building / unit / technology in that player's skin Disaster disaster string text, with tokens parsed Tokens inside strings (also inside localized texts): {a.N} (the N-th element argument), {b.<building type>} , {d.<disaster>} , {r.<resource>} (food, wood, stone, gold, hammer, culture, military, disaster), {o.<icon>} (hungry, scoreboard, research, question-mark, ship, population, clean-tile). Unknown tokens are dropped. In a C# interpolated string the token braces must be doubled: $"{player} got 5 {{r.gold}}" . Other elements: Localized(key, args) , OtherIcon (AI, CLEAN_TILE, DISCONNECTED, HOST, HUNGRY, POPULATION, QUESTION_MARK, RESEARCH, SHIP, ATTACK_POWER, SHIELD, SCOREBOARD).
docs.title: Text: StructuredText

docs.text: Tooltips: add HasToolTip to a UI object and set .text (a StructuredText ); shown after 0.4 s. Dialogs: ConfirmModal.OpenConfirm(icon, description, onCancel, onConfirm, dontShowAgainId) and OpenInformation(icon, description, onUnderstood, dontShowAgainId) : the game's own dialog, reusable. Game log: Log is networked. Log.AddMessage(StructuredText) works on the server only (a client just logs a warning); the entry syncs to every client, so a host-side mod can post messages everybody sees. Rows are visible 30 s and fade in 1 s. Chat ( ChatInterface ): Enter opens the field and disables the other input maps; sending calls Player.Local.Chat(text) (the host adds it to the log). While chat is open every chat and log row stays visible, and fades again 1 s after closing.
docs.title: Tooltips, dialogs, game log, chat

docs.text: Timer: turn number and ceil(time remaining) ( TimeRemaining while ACTIVE, TimeRemainingSync while SYNC; empty without a limit). The clock hand: Start / Harvest 0°, Disasters 90°, Build 180°, Combat 270°. A tick sound plays for each of the last 4 seconds ; a "waiting for you" sound plays once after 2 s when the others are ready and you are not. Ready button: click = TurnPhase.PhaseData(myIsland).Skip() . Clickable only while the phase is ACTIVE, after the 2 s banner, when you are not ready yet and the phase allows skipping. If the phase already considers you ready, it skips by itself. Phase banner: slides in from 1024 px above, leaves after 2 s ( disappearAfter , which is also BannerDuration ), switched off at 2.5 s. Changing disappearAfter also changes when Ready becomes clickable. Imminent victory warning: on every phase start (not the Win phase) WinPhase.CheckWin() is evaluated; if the predicted winner changed, or during every Build phase while a Wonder win is pending, the warning shows for 6 s and fades in the last 1 s. Counters (57 animated numbers) move toward their target at |target − value| × 2 + 10 per second.
docs.title: Timer, Ready, banners

docs.text: Harvest ( HarvestInterface ): one Dice per housing building, a "keep" and a "re-roll" grid; clicking a die moves it. The face is decided by the game before the throw, so a mod that changes yields afterwards does not change the face shown. Combat planning ( CombatInterface ): a slider per unit family, the ship "ghost" ( shipPreview ) and ClosestValidDebarkTransform for the landing preview. No ghost on your own island. Scoreboard (Tab): win conditions (military: defeated / total; wonder: own vs best other, missing resources, win delay), ping, resources, population, technologies. Send-resource arrows : 1 per click, Shift 5, Ctrl 10, capped by what you have → BuildData.SendResources . Shown only in the Build phase, when you are not defeated, for other players (teammates only in team games), and only with an available Market (active, not placed this phase). Player list ( PlayerSummary ): attack / defence power, population, connection, disaster log; click = fly to that island. TechTreeInterface is data-driven ( TechTree , IsTechnologyLearnt/Learnable/DemoLocked , StoredResources , OnClickTechnology , then Populate() ) and can be reused for a mod's own tree. WinInterface : victory visual, Continue / Exit / Discord / Steam buttons, gold gained. StartInterface : placer + selector for the start buildings.
docs.title: Screens

docs.text: SettingSetInterface.GenerateElements ( 0x54D2F0 ) builds the settings window by reflection over a SettingSet : an optional header ( settings.<set>.header.<key> ), then for every setting a row labelled settings.<set>.setting.<name> with a widget chosen by the setting's value type : bool → toggle, float → slider (range from the setting), enums ( FullScreenMode , Language , Quality , TimerSpeed ) and ScreenResolution → drop-down, input path → key rebinding (keyboard keys only), lobby code. An unknown type throws. So a new field of a supported type on a SettingSet appears in the game's own window (it needs the localization keys).

docs.text: Lobby, menus and Steam Main menu MainMenu.Awake ( 0x532D60 ): Button Does Training solo match with the tutorial Solo hosts locally with your own inventory, no Steam lobby Matchmaking starts or cancels the search Custom game opens the custom game window (pre-fills a lobby code from the clipboard) → Create SteamMatchmaking.CreateLobbyAsync(12) and host it → Join code find the lobby with that code and join → Join friend opens the Steam friends overlay Discord / Steam open the Discord invite / the store page About, Settings, Rules, Store toggle that window Exit quit At start the menu syncs time with NTP servers (for lobby keep-alive timestamps) and leaves a Steam lobby it was still in. MainMenu.Update runs every 0.1 s: friends, matchmaking, joining. While matchmaking or joining, Training, Solo and Custom game are disabled. Join errors: "Lobby not found.", "Inventory not found.", "Failed retrieving inventory: ...", "Cannot join a lobby with a different version.", "Canceled.". Matchmaking UpdateMatchmaking ( 0x539F70 ): Every 1 s, query Steam lobbies with the same version , matchmaking = True and progress = p (preparing). Drop lobbies that are not alive: keep-alive is an NTP timestamp, alive if within 10 s of now. None left: create an own invisible lobby (8 members) and wait in it. Otherwise pick the best by 2 × members, +1 if I own it, −100 if not alive , and switch only to a better one, so waiting players merge into the biggest lobby. The owner starts the match when the members agree on a host (each member's connected-to data votes), or when the lobby has at least 2 members and either the wait is at least (6 − members) × 150 s (2 players: 10 min, 5 players: 2.5 min, 6+: at once) or every member set matchmaking_start_anyways . Custom lobby The owner sets the lobby to friends-only, 12 members, and writes version , matchmaking , players ( P<own SteamId> ), progress = p and keep-alive . The game scene loads at once; the lobby is then the in-game StartGame panel: Rows: humans with Steam avatar and name, a Ready toggle (not for the host), host icon; AIs with name and difficulty drop-down (host only); colour and civilization; a "next colour" button (own row, only without teams) and a "next civilization" button (own row; the castle click, Player.NextCivilization ); kick (host only, not in matchmaking). Teams on: rows are grouped under team headers and the host re-slots players per team. Buttons: lobby settings (only the host may edit), Play (host; enabled when every player is an AI, the host, or Ready), Add AI, Invite friends. All hidden in matchmaking. Match start GameState.UpdateInit ( 0x5F69F0 ) → StartGame ( 0x5F50E0 ): Spawn the islands ( World layout ). Wait until every human has loaded every island and all island meshes are generated. GameStarted = true , turn counter = 1, StartGameRPC . Fewer than 2 human players → the timer is forced to UNLIMITED. onStartGame , then the host enters the start phase. Leaving: the win screen's Continue keeps you as a spectator; "Back to menu" asks for confirmation ( information.back-to-menu ); closing the game while networking first shuts the network down. Lobby settings LobbySettings : SettingSet : lobbyCode , timerSpeed (FAST / SLOW / UNLIMITED), multiMeteor , teams , wonderVictory . Defaults: FAST, multi-meteor off, teams off, wonder victory on. Synced to clients through GameState.lobbySettingsNetworked . The lobby code is 7 characters from ABCDEFGHJKMPQRST23456789 . Steam lobby keys MainMenu.LobbyConsts : Key Values version game version (must match to join) players AI<name> / P<SteamId> entries progress p preparing, r running, e ended keep-alive heartbeat timestamp written by the owner connected-to host vote (member data) matchmaking , matchmaking_start_anyways , matchmaking_fill_ai quick-match flags member / player_<SteamId> per-player value code lobby code Rich presence ( RichPresenceConsts ): connect , status = MAIN_MENU / SEARCHING / IN_LOBBY / IN_GAME, game_type = training / solo / quick-match / custom-game, turn , steam_display , steam_player_group(_size) . Inventory and civilizations Steam item definitions: Id Name Meaning 11001 GOLD in-game currency item 11002 GOLD_PACK a pack of gold 12002 GOLD_PACK_BUNDLE a bundle of packs Item properties set on Steam's side: dice_kingdoms_unlocks_civilization (a civilization name) and dice_kingdoms_drop_when ( GAME_START or QUICK_MATCH_VICTORY ). PlayerInventory.FromSteamworks ( 0x56E170 ): every owned item with the unlock property gives its civilization ( UnlockedCivilizations ). Nothing → FALLBACK = [EUROPE], so Europe is always available. The demo build always uses the fallback. Joiners: the client sends its serialized Steam inventory as connection data; the host deserializes it ( SteamInventory.DeserializeAsync ) and rejects it if expired or if it belongs to someone else. So a client cannot claim civilizations it does not own; a modified host can give its own players anything. At spawn ( Player.NetworkStart 0x56FBA0 , host): colour = random among the free ones, civilization = random among the unlocked ones , start slot = first free of 0..11. In the lobby, Player.NextCivilization ( 0x570500 , host, before the start) cycles through the unlocked civilizations. See Rules and civilizations for what not to patch. Item drops and the store Game start drops ( MainMenu.CheckManualDrops ): eligible GAME_START items are requested with SteamInventory.AddPromoItemAsync ; Steam decides if they are granted. Quick-match victory drops ( RegisterWinReward ): only when the match lasted at least 5 turns and the winner is on your team . The gold gained (item 11001 before/after) is shown on the win screen. Store.CanBeBought(item) : the item has a price (bought in the Steam overlay) or a Steam exchange recipe (bought with gold). Purchases are done by Steam. Drops and gold come from Steam's servers; a mod cannot create them. For local testing a postfix on PlayerInventory.FromSteamworks can add civilizations in solo games and when you host.

docs.text: Meteorites and castle protection The logic is in Meteorite.<Execute>d__4.MoveNext (state 0), decompiled from game version 1.0.4. The Meteorite object has these integer fields: Field Meaning radius Radius of the impact in tiles. minimumCastleTiles Minimum number of castle tiles inside the radius for a hit on the castle to be accepted. meteoriteTilesToFullyAllowHitCastle The "castle protection limit" (T below). All three are read live for every meteor and are not clamped by the game. A limit such as 1000 in a mod's settings is the mod's own clamp, not the game's. Choosing the impact tile scorched = IslandGrid.CountGround(grid, 5) : the number of scorched earth tiles (ground tile 5). One random roll per meteor: roll is uniform in [0, T) , computed as (uint)(random.state * (int)T) >> 32 . Up to 256 times: pick a random grass tile, count the castle tiles inside the radius ( IslandGrid.MeteoriteNumberCastleTiles , castle tiles with squared distance at most radius^2 ), and accept the pick if castleTiles <= 0 , or if scorched > roll and castleTiles >= minimumCastleTiles . If all 256 picks were rejected, the last pick is used anyway. Consequences The castle can be hit with a probability of min(1, scorched / T) . T = 0 protects the castle only while there are no scorched tiles (protection for the first meteor). A huge T (up to int.MaxValue ) makes a hit on the castle practically impossible. What the impact does IslandGrid.MeteoriteDisaster : for tiles within the radius that are inside the island limit ( HardLimit.IsWithin ): skip ground tile 1; remove inner cliffs if the ground is 4; set the ground to 5 (scorched earth); apply the disaster to or remove the buildings there; add the nature object 3 (lava).

docs.text: Networking Model Host-authoritative MLAPI over Steam P2P. The host (lobby owner) is the MLAPI server and also a client; the other players are clients. Clients only send intents . The server checks them, applies the rules, rolls every random number and sends the results (ClientRPCs and NetworkedVar s). Phase logic ( TurnPhase.Update , Sync , ApplyChanges ) and the AI run only where IsServer is true. Random results are either rolled on the server (dice, disaster selection) or come from seeds the server sends (disaster occurrences, the per-island generator, combat). Combat is simulated on every client from the same deployment list with software floats and a fixed tick, and a per-tick hash is logged to catch desyncs. There is no separate anti-cheat. Utility.AntiCheat.EncryptedStorage only hides the resource values in memory ( Harvest ). Mods and multiplayer A rule change must run on the host to take effect for everybody. A change made only on a client changes that client's display, and it can desync the combat simulation, which every client runs itself. Player.initialOwnerId ( NetworkedVar<ulong> 0xC8 ) is set by the host in Player.NetworkStart and never changes: humans = their client id, AIs = fake ids counting down from ulong.MaxValue . It is the player's identity for the whole match, also after a reconnect. Player.Local = the player with initialOwnerId == LocalClientId . Player name ( Player.UpdateUserName 0x570DC0 ) AI: " " (for example "Red Peasant"); human: the Steam name, unless the console's cinematic mode is on (then the colour name) Lobby list Steam avatar, friend state, rich presence ( FriendVisual ) Steam lobby data players ( AI<name> / P<id> ), player_<SteamId> keys at game start, member data matchmaking_fill_ai Main menu friends list, invites, join requests, rich presence Places where it is only an identity (any stable, unique number works): join approval, reconnect and rejoin (players are matched by InitialOwnerId ), disconnects, kicks, the host marker ( InitialOwnerId == GameState.OwnerClientId ), per-player lookups. (lobby key version ). AutoHost ( NetworkingManager.StartHost() in Start ) is a leftover developer component, not placed in the shipped scenes. docs.text: Host-authoritative MLAPI over Steam P2P. The host (lobby owner) is the MLAPI server and also a client; the other players are clients. Clients only send intents . The server checks them, applies the rules, rolls every random number and sends the results (ClientRPCs and NetworkedVar s). Phase logic ( TurnPhase.Update , Sync , ApplyChanges ) and the AI run only where IsServer is true. Random results are either rolled on the server (dice, disaster selection) or come from seeds the server sends (disaster occurrences, the per-island generator, combat). Combat is simulated on every client from the same deployment list with software floats and a fixed tick, and a per-tick hash is logged to catch desyncs. There is no separate anti-cheat. Utility.AntiCheat.EncryptedStorage only hides the resource values in memory ( Harvest ). Mods and multiplayer A rule change must run on the host to take effect for everybody. A change made only on a client changes that client's display, and it can desync the combat simulation, which every client runs itself.

docs.text: Overview Engine and libraries Unity 2021.3.36f1 , HDRP (High Definition Render Pipeline), IL2CPP , Windows x64. Burst and the Job System are used for island generation and combat pathfinding. Networking: MLAPI (the old Unity Netcode, MLAPI.Runtime.dll ): NetworkedBehaviour , NetworkedVar<T> , NetworkedList<T> , [ServerRPC] / [ClientRPC] . The transport is Steam P2P . See Networking . Steam: Fivemid.FiveSteam.dll , a fork of Facepunch.Steamworks (namespaces Steamworks , Steamworks.Data , Steamworks.Ugc , Steamworks.ServerList ) plus wrappers in Utility.Steamworks . Fivemid.FiveTime.dll (time helpers), Utility.dll (the developers' shared utilities: pooling, noise, splines, silhouettes, taskbar flash, AntiCheat.EncryptedStorage ), Utility.SoftFloat.dll (deterministic software float sfloat ). Other libraries: A* Pathfinding Project, Addressables, Unity Localization (6 languages), TextMeshPro, the new Input System, Timeline, VFX Graph, Tayx.Graphy (FPS overlay), CommandTerminal (the in-game developer console, see Developer console ), Backtrace.Unity (crash reports), Newtonsoft.Json. Assembly-CSharp.dll is almost empty. All game code is in DiceKingdoms.dll . Crash reports Backtrace sends crash reports (with minidumps) to the developers. A crash caused by a mod reaches them too. Namespaces Namespace Types Contents DiceKingdoms.Game 336 Rules and simulation: GameState , phases, Island / IslandGrid , buildings, resources, technologies, combat, disasters, AI, players, lobby settings DiceKingdoms.Interface 274 In-match UI and visuals: buttons, phase interfaces, dice, camera, building placer, tooltips, StructuredText DiceKingdoms.Meta 149 Outside the match: main menu, matchmaking, store, rules screen, settings, developer cheats, version, Steam items DiceKingdoms.Network 34 MLAPI serializers for the game types, snapshots, AutoHost , spawn handlers, NetRef DiceKingdoms.Environment 11 Clouds, day/night cycle, seagulls, quality toggles Scenes The addressable scenes are Scenes/MainMenu and Scenes/SteamMultiplayer . A match runs in SteamMultiplayer . Settings files <game folder>/GameSettings/*.json : audio.json , game.json (language), input.json (key bindings as Input System paths, for example rotate /Keyboard/r , mirror /Keyboard/t , keep placing /Keyboard/shift , scoreboard /Keyboard/tab ) and video.json . Audio, game and input are stored in Steam Cloud when Steam runs; video is local only. Details: Audio, settings and localization . Useful constants GameState.MAX_PLAYERS = 12 . Steam app id 1501690 . The update check calls https://api.steamcmd.net/v1/info/{appid} and compares the depot branches. The About window shows {0} - build #{1} on branch {2} ( LocalVersion asset + Version struct). Conventions on these pages Class, method and field names are from the IL2CPP dump (Il2CppDumper). They are stable between updates; addresses and offsets are not . Addresses are RVAs in GameAssembly.dll of game version 1.0.4 . In Ghidra (or any tool that loads the DLL at its preferred base) the address is 0x180000000 + RVA . Generic methods ( TurnPhase<,> , PhaseData<,> ) share one compiled body for reference types ( TurnPhase<object,object> ); its RVA is listed under the generic method in dump.cs . Standard IL2CPP layouts: object header 0x10 ; array length +0x18 , data +0x20 ; string length +0x10 , UTF-16 characters +0x14 ; List<T> items +0x10 , size +0x18 . Struct field offsets in dump.cs are given without the header. "Confirmed in game" means the behaviour was also checked in a live match; everything else was read in the decompiled code.

docs.text: Rendering, visuals and animation Pipeline HDRP , two pipeline assets for the two quality levels ( HDRenderPipelineAsset-Low , -Normal ; Normal is the default). Volume profiles: Common , Day , Night , Altitude , Low , Normal . One perspective camera Viewport (FOV 45, near 0.1, far 1000) renders the world and the UI (see Interface behaviour ). Game shaders are HDRP Shader Graphs: ColoredPaper (almost everything), Flag , Sail , Water , Windy (vegetation), Particle , SolidColor , Silhouette Object . The palette ("colored paper") Buildings, units, ships and props use the ColoredPaper shader ( _ColorPalette , _EmissionPalette , _ColorTint , _EmissionTint , _EmissionFactor , _Scale ). Meshes have no colour textures : their UVs point into one 8×8 palette ( ColorPalette.png ), and each face takes the colour of one cell (use point filtering when you look at exported models). Lit windows use the emission palette (cells (5,0) orange and (5,1) yellow are the only emissive ones). Player and team colours PlayerColors.Init ( 0x56DD40 ) makes one PlayerColor per colour. Its constructor copies the palette texture and repaints cell (7, 7) with the player's colour ( CustomColorPalette ). Faces that show the owner's colour have their UVs on cell (7, 7). On the Castle that is the flag and the King's clothes; the castle body itself has none. ColoredPaperUtils.set_PlayerColor puts the player's palette on all renderers of an object and sets its outline colour; BuildingVisual.Apply does this for every building, and units, ships and inhabitants use the same helper. Colour (palette cell) Group Red (1,6), Pink (3,2), Orange (1,5) 0 Green (1,2), Carribean (4,7), Cyan (2,3) 1 Yellow (1,3), Ivory (0,5), Brown (0,3) 2 Blue (2,4), Grey (4,5), Purple (3,3) 3 colorsPerTeam = 3 : 12 colours in 4 groups . Colours can be picked freely in both modes. The group only matters when the lobby option Teams is on: then Team.Same(a, b) = same group. In free-for-all Team.Same is true only for the same player. A new colour list must stay a multiple of 3. ColoredPaperOverrides replaces a renderer's materials with cached clones keyed by (base material, palette, colour tint, emission tint). Buildings Prefab parts: Visual , Damaged Visual (a copy of the mesh), Fires (3 fire particle systems), Damage Particles , Remains particles, onlyEnableWhenActive objects. State What changes Tint ( BuildingTints ) normal – none hungry (starvation) inhabitant replaced by a ragdoll brown (0.5, 0.284, 0.074, 0.85) sick / any other disaster inhabitant replaced by a ragdoll green (0.133, 0.4, 0.067, 0.85) destroyed (health ≤ 0) Visual off, Damaged Visual on and sinks ; first time a particle burst (size × 30) burnt, dark blue-grey (0.149, 0.169, 0.267, 1) Fires follow the building's health. Sinking: the remains sink to the average over their tiles of −0.3 − 0.2 × distance to the coast (further inland sinks deeper), moved with SmoothDamp (0.2 s smooth time, about 90 % after 0.8 s). Units killed in combat become ragdolls with the deathInCombatTint (0.635, 0.257, 0.297, 0.6), pushed along the hit direction. onlyEnableWhenActive : the inhabitant of Barracks, Castle, Church, Cottage, House and Sorcerer Tower (and the chimney smoke on some of them) is shown only while the building is active, so a hungry or sick building loses its smoke. The other 90 building prefabs have nothing in this list. Placing: no grow animation, only a particle burst ( BuildingVisual.OnPlace , footprint tiles × 5 particles). Hit: hit sound + 10 damage particles. BuildingVisual.ApplyLater(building, grid, delay) applies a state change at the right moment of a phase animation. Outline: Utility.Silhouette , a custom HDRP pass with a stencil shader; colour = player colour, or the tile cursor colour. Day and night DayNightCycle ( DiceKingdoms.Environment ), ApplyTimeOfDay ( 0x57CC70 ): Sun rotation = (timeOfDay × 360°, sunYaw, 0); k = sunIntensity(timeOfDay) × (1 − cloudiness) ; sun intensity = k × max. Day volume weight = k, Night volume weight = 1 − k. sunIntensity : 0 → 0, 0.05 → 0.8, 0.25 → 1, 0.45 → 0.8, 0.5 → 0, 1 → 0. Day is 0 – 0.5, night 0.5 – 1. timeOfDay moves forward only toward targetTimeOfDay (wrapping past 1), smoothing 1 per second; cloudiness smoothing 5. Every phase sets the time of day when it starts: TurnPhase.Enter writes the phase's timeOfDay field into the target. All phases have 0.125 (morning, sun 45° up), so the game always shows morning, and the night half (Night profile, night ambience) is built but unused. Lightning and Thunderstorm darken the sky: target cloudiness 1, wait until it is above 0.9, strike, then back to 0. Night or per-phase light TimeOfDay = 0.75f on Object.FindObjectOfType<DayNightCycle>() gives midnight, but only until the next phase starts (confirmed in game). Re-apply it in a postfix on TurnPhase.Enter , or change each phase's timeOfDay field once at match start; that also allows a different light per phase. It is a local visual, safe in multiplayer. The night profile looks quite washed out on the colourful models. Building orientation and the camera GridTransform.Apply ( 0x60F050 ): GridTransform = tile position , orientation 0..3, mirroring . Orientations: 0 EAST, 1 NORTH, 2 WEST, 3 SOUTH . Each step turns the model 90° counter-clockwise seen from above . Mirroring flips the local X scale. The model's pivot is the centre of the building's tile (0, 0); grid y = Unity Z. Islands are never rotated. The camera yaw is fixed at 45° : it always looks toward Unity +X +Z, so you only ever see the south and west sides of a building. Only height and pitch change. There is no door or entrance concept in the code; units leave from ships, never from buildings. Castle gates of the original models (side at orientation 0): Europe and Middle East east (seen at orientations 2 and 3), Viking and Ancient west (seen at 0 and 1), Maya on all sides. A Castle placed automatically gets orientation 0 (EAST is tried first), so Europe and Middle East show their back unless the player turns it with R. AI castles use a random start orientation. The big flag ( flag_big ) has the same rotation in every castle prefab and turns with the building. Visual effects All effects are pooled , free themselves and are client-side only ; the game logic is driven by the disaster coroutines and combat ticks, the visuals follow. Visual Used by Behaviour Values FireVisual Fire, Tornado particle shape fitted to the building bounds, burst = tiles × 5, sound fades in / out duration 3, sound fade 0.5 LightningVisual Lightning, Thunderstorm random zig-zag bolt in a cone (bones tilted up to ±90°, retried until it fits) duration 0.2, max distance 3 TornadoVisual Tornado grows and shrinks, spins 200 °/s, funnel 1000 °/s, tilted −30° duration 2.5 MeteoriteVisual Meteorite flies a straight line from 90 m away at 45° elevation with a random yaw , 30 m/s, for 3 s; the crater is applied 3.2 s after the start TsunamiVisual Tsunami animated wave (clip 3.683 s), per-tile splashes, freed after 4 s Projectiles ( ProjectileVisual ): Arrow / Archer arrow (gravity 0.6, friction 0.01, length 0.43), Fireball (gravity 0.2, friction 0.001). The motion is ballistic with linear drag, solved exactly so the projectile lands on the combat tick its hit is resolved: p(t) = start + (V × (1 − e^(−k t)) + g t) / k . At most 256 at once. Harvest icons ( HarvestedResourceVisual ): grow in 0.15 s, fly freely for 0.5 s (start 1200 px/s at ±45°), then a "magnet" pulls them at 2000 px/s to their counter (collected within 40 px). The harvest phase waits at least 1.5 s for them. Dice Dice.Roll(destination, faceUp) ( 0x5C16A0 ) pre-simulates a whole physical-looking throw (gravity −10, bounce 0.8 with 0.4 randomness, start velocity (−0.6, 0, 0) ± 0.1, angular 30, from height 0.1), then rotates it so the face that ends on top is faceUp (decided by the game) and shifts it to destination . The die first glides 1 s to the start pose. Each bounce plays a sound with volume = bounce strength (if ≥ 0.02). The throw only shows a result that is already known. Animation timings Unit clips (seconds; every unit uses one controller with per-unit overrides): Unit Idle Walk Run Attack Peasant, Bourgeois, Soldier, Templar, General, King 1.3 1.3 0.633 0.433 Archer 1.3 1.3 0.633 1.333 Priest 1.3 1.3 0.633 1.3 Sorcerer, Warlock 1.3 1.3 0.633 1.3 (Europe 0.8) Maya clips are 1.25 × longer. Transitions: into attack 0.1 s, exit at 87 % of the attack; others 0.25 s. Inhabitants walk at 0.288 and run at 1.06 units/s. Thing Value Ship plank out / in 0.8 s (Europe, Middle East), 0.667 s (others) Soldiers leave the ship after landing ( DEBARK_DELAY ) 5 ticks (0.5 s) Windmill turn 2.33 – 3.97 s per civilization Combat tick 0.1 s, max 3000 ticks Phase banner 2 s (+0.5 s to switch off) Tooltip delay 0.4 s Log row 30 s visible, 1 s fade Victory warning 6 s, 1 s fade Music crossfade 2 s Camera pitch by height 0 → 0°, 4 → −30°, 25 → −55°, 100 → −90° Tips Recolour one object: ColoredPaperUtils.SlowTint(transform, tint) / SlowSetPlayerColor(transform, color) . New models: put player-coloured faces on palette cell (7, 7) and use the ColoredPaper material so tints and player colours work. See Custom models . Effects are visual only: changing prefab values (durations, particles) is safe in multiplayer. For the meteorite keep the 3.2 s wait longer than the 3 s fall.

Day volume weight = k, Night volume weight = 1 − k. sunIntensity : 0 → 0, 0.05 → 0.8, 0.25 → 1, 0.45 → 0.8, 0.5 → 0, 1 → 0. Day is 0 – 0.5, night 0.5 – 1. timeOfDay moves forward only toward targetTimeOfDay (wrapping past 1), smoothing 1 per second; cloudiness smoothing 5. Every phase sets the time of day when it starts: TurnPhase.Enter writes the phase's timeOfDay field into the target. All phases have 0.125 (morning, sun 45° up), so the game always shows morning, and the night half (Night profile, night ambience) is built but unused. Lightning and Thunderstorm darken the sky: target cloudiness 1, wait until it is above 0.9, strike, then back to 0. Night or per-phase light TimeOfDay = 0.75f on Object.FindObjectOfType<DayNightCycle>() gives midnight, but only until the next phase starts (confirmed in game). Re-apply it in a postfix on TurnPhase.Enter , or change each phase's timeOfDay field once at match start; that also allows a different light per phase. It is a local visual, safe in multiplayer. The night profile looks quite washed out on the colourful models.
docs.title: Day and night

docs.text: GridTransform.Apply ( 0x60F050 ): GridTransform = tile position , orientation 0..3, mirroring . Orientations: 0 EAST, 1 NORTH, 2 WEST, 3 SOUTH . Each step turns the model 90° counter-clockwise seen from above . Mirroring flips the local X scale. The model's pivot is the centre of the building's tile (0, 0); grid y = Unity Z. Islands are never rotated. The camera yaw is fixed at 45° : it always looks toward Unity +X +Z, so you only ever see the south and west sides of a building. Only height and pitch change. There is no door or entrance concept in the code; units leave from ships, never from buildings. Castle gates of the original models (side at orientation 0): Europe and Middle East east (seen at orientations 2 and 3), Viking and Ancient west (seen at 0 and 1), Maya on all sides. A Castle placed automatically gets orientation 0 (EAST is tried first), so Europe and Middle East show their back unless the player turns it with R. AI castles use a random start orientation. The big flag ( flag_big ) has the same rotation in every castle prefab and turns with the building.
docs.title: Building orientation and the camera

docs.text: All effects are pooled , free themselves and are client-side only ; the game logic is driven by the disaster coroutines and combat ticks, the visuals follow. Visual Used by Behaviour Values FireVisual Fire, Tornado particle shape fitted to the building bounds, burst = tiles × 5, sound fades in / out duration 3, sound fade 0.5 LightningVisual Lightning, Thunderstorm random zig-zag bolt in a cone (bones tilted up to ±90°, retried until it fits) duration 0.2, max distance 3 TornadoVisual Tornado grows and shrinks, spins 200 °/s, funnel 1000 °/s, tilted −30° duration 2.5 MeteoriteVisual Meteorite flies a straight line from 90 m away at 45° elevation with a random yaw , 30 m/s, for 3 s; the crater is applied 3.2 s after the start TsunamiVisual Tsunami animated wave (clip 3.683 s), per-tile splashes, freed after 4 s Projectiles ( ProjectileVisual ): Arrow / Archer arrow (gravity 0.6, friction 0.01, length 0.43), Fireball (gravity 0.2, friction 0.001). The motion is ballistic with linear drag, solved exactly so the projectile lands on the combat tick its hit is resolved: p(t) = start + (V × (1 − e^(−k t)) + g t) / k . At most 256 at once. Harvest icons ( HarvestedResourceVisual ): grow in 0.15 s, fly freely for 0.5 s (start 1200 px/s at ±45°), then a "magnet" pulls them at 2000 px/s to their counter (collected within 40 px). The harvest phase waits at least 1.5 s for them.
docs.title: Visual effects

docs.text: Dice.Roll(destination, faceUp) ( 0x5C16A0 ) pre-simulates a whole physical-looking throw (gravity −10, bounce 0.8 with 0.4 randomness, start velocity (−0.6, 0, 0) ± 0.1, angular 30, from height 0.1), then rotates it so the face that ends on top is faceUp (decided by the game) and shifts it to destination . The die first glides 1 s to the start pose. Each bounce plays a sound with volume = bounce strength (if ≥ 0.02). The throw only shows a result that is already known.

docs.text: Resources Resource Resources in the game are represented by the DiceKingdoms.Game.Resource enum: namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; public enum Resource { FOOD , WOOD , STONE , GOLD , HAMMER , CULTURE , MILITARY , DISASTER } The enum values act as identifiers: the code uses them to address a resource in indexers, arrays, and lists, pass it to methods, and serialize it in network messages. ResourceAmount Resource amounts are represented by the DiceKingdoms.Game.ResourceAmount struct: namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [Serializable] [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit)] public struct ResourceAmount { [FieldOffset(0)] public int food ; [FieldOffset(4)] public int wood ; [FieldOffset(8)] public int stone ; [FieldOffset(12)] public int gold ; [FieldOffset(16)] public int hammer ; [FieldOffset(20)] public int culture ; [FieldOffset(24)] public int military ; [FieldOffset(28)] public int disaster ; public static ResourceAmount ZERO { get ; set ; } public int this [ Resource resource ] { get ; set ; } public int Total { get ; } public override bool Equals ( ResourceAmount other ); public override bool Equals ( object obj ); public override int GetHashCode (); public override string ToString (); public static ResourceAmount operator + ( ResourceAmount a ); public static ResourceAmount operator - ( ResourceAmount a ); public static ResourceAmount operator + ( ResourceAmount a , ResourceAmount b ); public static ResourceAmount operator - ( ResourceAmount a , ResourceAmount b ); public static ResourceAmount operator * ( int a , ResourceAmount b ); public static bool operator >= ( ResourceAmount a , ResourceAmount b ); public static bool operator <= ( ResourceAmount a , ResourceAmount b ); public static bool operator == ( ResourceAmount a , ResourceAmount b ); public static bool operator != ( ResourceAmount a , ResourceAmount b ); public static ResourceAmount Max ( ResourceAmount a , ResourceAmount b ); public static ResourceAmount Min ( ResourceAmount a , ResourceAmount b ); } The indexer by Resource allows reading and writing the amount of a specific resource through the enum, e.g. amount[Resource.WOOD] . Binary and unary + and - are supported, along with multiplication by an int on the left ( int * ResourceAmount ). Operators >= , <= , == , != - there are no separate < and > . The Max and Min methods return the component-wise maximum and minimum of two ResourceAmount values. The Total property returns the sum of all resources. The static ZERO is a constant with all fields set to zero. ResourceStorage The player's resource storage is represented by the DiceKingdoms.Game.ResourceStorage struct: namespace DiceKingdoms.Game ; [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Explicit)] public struct ResourceStorage { [FieldOffset(0)] public readonly ResourceAmount stored ; [FieldOffset(32)] public readonly ResourceAmount capacity ; public ResourceStorage ( ResourceAmount stored , ResourceAmount capacity ); public ResourceStorage WithCapacity ( ResourceAmount capacity ); public ResourceStorage WithStored ( ResourceAmount stored ); public override string ToString (); } Two ResourceAmount fields - stored (the current amount of resources) and capacity (the storage's capacity). Both fields are declared readonly, making the struct immutable: once created, its state cannot be changed. WithCapacity returns a copy with the capacity replaced, WithStored — a copy with the stored amount replaced. The original instance remains unchanged. ResourceStorageInterface A single resource storage widget is represented by the DiceKingdoms.Interface.ResourceStorageInterface class: namespace DiceKingdoms.Interface ; public class ResourceStorageInterface : MonoBehaviour { public ColorPalette colorPalette ; public Resource resource ; public Counter counterStored ; public Counter counterCapacity ; public Counter counterGain ; public Image icon ; public Ripple ripple ; public RectTransform counters ; public Sound incrementSound ; public Interface @interface ; public Resource Resource { get ; } public int Stored { get ; set ; } public int Capacity { get ; set ; } public int? Gain { get ; set ; } public Image Icon { get ; } protected void Awake (); protected void OnEnable (); protected void OnDisable (); protected void Update (); private void SetValuesFromIsland (); public void Increment ( int value ); } This is a UI component for a single storage slot in the harvest panel ( HarvestInterface ). HarvestInterfac e holds an array of eight such widgets - one for each resource in the Resource enum - and uses them to display the storage values. Ten public fields bound in the prefab via the Unity Inspector: colorPalette , resource (the resource type this widget is responsible for), three counters counterStored / counterCapacity / counterGain (a custom UI component Counter), icon (resource icon), ripple , counters (a RectTransform container for the counters), incrementSound (gain sound), and @interface (a reference to the main Interface). SetValuesFromIsland() - private, synchronizes the widget's values with the current storage state on the island. Increment(int value) - public, animates a resource gain: plays a sound and triggers a ripple effect.

docs.text: Reverse-engineering notes Version Addresses and offsets below are from game version 1.0.4. They change with every game update. Prefer names and fields from the interop assemblies when you can, and use offsets only for hooks you check against your build. Method Il2CppDumper produces dump.cs with all classes, fields and method RVAs. Its naming for methods is Namespace.Class$$MethodName . Ghidra with GameAssembly.dll loaded: the Ghidra address is 0x180000000 + RVA (for example 180616890 is RVA 0x616890 ). Standard il2cpp layouts: array length at +0x18 and data at +0x20 ; string length at +0x10 and UTF-16 characters at +0x14 ; List<T>._size at +0x18 . Island Item Value IslandGrid.size (int2) 0xF0 IslandGrid.generationParameters 0x1E8 ( HardLimit.radius at +0 , default 22) IslandGrid.Awake RVA 0x6130C0 IslandGrid.CanPlaceBuilding 0x6143A0 IslandGrid.ImportIsland (private) 0x616340 IslandGrid.ExportIsland 0x614900 IslandGrid.Generate / GenerateJob 0x614EB0 / 0x614D90 IslandGrid.MeteoriteDisaster 0x616890 IslandGrid.MeteoriteNumberCastleTiles 0x616DF0 Island.grid / owner 0x98 / 0x90 The radius of the island can be changed in the Awake hook; real land is then produced by normal generation. Resizing arrays does not work. SaveIslandToClipboard ( 0x61A690 ) and LoadIslandFromClipboard ( 0x616810 ) go through GUIUtility.systemCopyBuffer , which is unreliable outside OnGUI ; use ExportIsland / ImportIsland and handle the clipboard yourself. The code format is in Island save format . Players and game state Item Value Player.UserName (string) 0x110 , getter 0x473BB0 Player.get_Island 0x508770 Player.get_StartGameReady 0x571AB0 PlayerSummary.island / attackers / gameState 0xD0 / 0xE8 / 0xC8 GameState.Island(Player) 0x5F2F60 Buildings Item Value BuildData.CanBuildType 0x628760 : IsBuildable , then Unlocked , then SteamDemo , then HasResource BuildData.CanRemoveNature 0x6288B0 : its own inline check, allows only trees, rocks, scorched earth and lava. It does not call NatureTile.Cleanable , so a hook on Cleanable has no effect. BuildData.CleanTile 0x628AB0 BuildingType.id +0x10 (this is the type id, not a category) BuildingType.localPositions / localPositionsInWater 0x18 / 0x20 BuildingType.tier / health (maximum) +0x78 / +0x80 BuildingType.get_DisplayName 0x5F0E10 BuildingTypes.get_Types 0x5717B0 (save-file order, alphabetical by name) The pickaxe tool ( CleanTileTool ) only works on the builder's own island and cannot remove water rocks, because those are ground tiles, not nature. Cheats Cheats.get_Available ( 0x52A840 ) and Cheats.CheckAvailable ( 0x528D40 ) return true when hooked, which unlocks the developer console commands. Meteorites See Meteorites and castle protection . Nature tile enum TREE = 0 , ROCK = 1 , SCORCHED_EARTH = 2 , LAVA = 3 , FLOWER = 4 , FISH = 5 .
docs.title: Reverse-Engineering Notes

docs.text: Rules and civilizations Rules screen The Rules screen ( Rules ) has an index on the left (How to Play, Game Phases, Buildings, Disasters, Units, Technologies) and a scroll view with the content. The Technologies tab shows the tech tree of the civilization chosen in the civilization drop-down. Rules.Awake fills the drop-down ( civilizationDropdown , a DiceKingdoms.Interface.Dropdown ) from Enum.GetValues(typeof(Civilization)) . Each entry is a tuple of a structured text and the boxed enum value. The wrapper keeps the boxed values in values and its TMP_Dropdown calls onSelect(values[index]) . Rules.OnSelectCivilization(object) unboxes a Civilization , sets PlayerSkins.Civilization and rebuilds the Technologies tab with Technologies.TechTree(civilization) . Technologies.TechTree(Civilization) is First(t => t.civilization == civ) over the game's own list, so it throws for an unknown civilization . Building cards ( Rules Building ) are 378x256, three to a row. Adding a civilization Every place the game uses a civilization number, and what it does with an unknown one, is listed in Civilizations in the game code ; the practical guide is Making a civilization . In short: answer TechTree(civilization) for that number (also where the compiler inlined it), let PlayerSkins and the network readers accept it (the number is one signed byte, so 5..127), give AIs a build order, make it selectable (the Rules drop-down and the castle click, below) and provide the per-civilization data the game looks up (skins, tech tree asset, name). Technologies.TechTree throws for an unknown civilization ( First over the game's list). A mod has to answer it for its own number, for example with the tree of the built-in civilization the new one is based on. PlayerSkins.Civilization 's setter derives the biome with a switch over 0..4 and throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for anything else, and so does the PlayerSkins constructor (the log reads Parameter name: civilization ). A new civilization must therefore be built for a built-in one first and the real number stored afterwards ( PlayerSkins.civilization field). Choosing a civilization for play (the castle click) On the match-start screen, clicking a player's castle runs Player.NextCivilization . On the host it steps through Player.Inventory.UnlockedCivilizations (the civilizations the player's Steam inventory has unlocked), wraps around, and sets Player.skins to new PlayerSkins(civilization, skinRegistry) ; a client sends NextCivilizationRPC to the host, which runs the same code. It does nothing once the player is ready ( StartGameReady ). Do not replace or patch the player's inventory Player.NetworkStart (host side, when a player is spawned) also picks the random starting civilization with RandomExtensions.NextSample<Civilization> from the same array, and a random colour with NextSample<PlayerColor> . NextSample indexes array[(state * length) >> 32] , so an empty array throws IndexOutOfRangeException . A mod that rebuilt PlayerInventory (a postfix on PlayerInventory.FromSteamworks , writing PlayerInventory.FALLBACK ) made the spawn throw: no player existed and the lobby screen showed only the top bar. Patching the UnlockedCivilizations getter instead crashed the game at start: it is a few bytes of native code that IL2CPP shares between identical getters. A safe place to add civilizations to the castle click is a prefix on Player.NextCivilization : after the last unlocked civilization, step through your own ones, then let the game wrap around. Scoreboard ScoreboardRow.Start creates the row's stat cells by cloning the first cell: ping, six resources, population and technologies, and a trailing empty cell. The row is Scoreboard Row(Clone) with a Name child (about 200 wide), the stat cells (about 96 wide) and the trailing empty Stat(Clone) , which holds the Button Send child. That button appears on the resource cells after a market is built, to send resources to other players. The board's frame grows by about 112 units for every cell that is added. The vanilla frame spans roughly x 269..1651 on a 1920 screen, so a mod column should take the place of the empty trailing cell instead of widening the board.
